title: LEC : échec des négociations avec Solary, Shifters finalement maintenu en 2027 ?
content:
Solary ne devrait finalement pas débarquer en LEC en 2027. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , la structure française aurait bien entamé des discussions avec Shifters pour récupérer temporairement sa place dans l’élite européenne de League of Legends. Mais les deux organisations ne seraient pas parvenues à trouver un accord. Un coup d’arrêt pour cette piste, alors que Shifters avait contacté plusieurs structures, notamment issues des ligues régionales européennes, afin d’étudier la possibilité de louer son slot.

La question financière aurait notamment représenté un obstacle majeur pour Solary. Son cofondateur Wakz avait récemment expliqué qu’une arrivée en LEC était « pas impossible, mais peu probable » , évoquant un investissement considérable. Selon ses estimations, le fonctionnement d’une équipe sur une saison coûterait environ un million d’euros, avec une marge de 300 000 euros. En ajoutant la location du slot, la facture totale pourrait grimper entre 2 et 5 millions d’euros. Un montant difficilement envisageable pour la structure tourangelle, qui avait déjà dû mobiliser 200 000 euros supplémentaires pour financer ses nouveaux locaux.

Face à cette situation, Shifters aurait décidé de reprendre les choses en main. Toujours selon Sheep Esports , son directeur général Mathieu Debonnaire aurait commencé à contacter des joueurs et leurs agents pour préparer la saison 2027. Le jungler français Sheo participerait également aux discussions autour du futur effectif, même si sa présence dans l’équipe n’est pas encore garantie. Tous les contrats des joueurs de la saison 2026 sont arrivés à expiration le 16 novembre.

Cette reprise des activités laisse donc penser que Shifters pourrait finalement conserver sa place en LEC, même si une location du slot reste théoriquement possible. L’organisation devra toutefois rattraper son retard sur un mercato déjà bien avancé, plusieurs concurrents ayant bouclé leur recrutement. Après une saison 2026 particulièrement difficile, conclue aux dernières places du championnat, Shifters pourrait ainsi repartir de zéro avec l’objectif de retrouver de la compétitivité en 2027.

title: The Game Awards 2026 Nominees: Full List of Every Category
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI leads The Game Awards 2026 nominees with eight nominations, including Game of the Year, after Geoff Keighley revealed the shortlist across all categories in a livestream on 17 November. Rockstar Games’ open world title earned its place two days before its own launch, with its release landing inside this year’s eligibility window by a single day.

CONTROL Resonant and Resident Evil Requiem follow with six nominations each, while Phantom Blade Zero has five. The ceremony takes place on 10 December 2026 at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, with Keighley hosting for the thirteenth time. A jury drawn from more than 160 media and creator outlets picked the nominees, and fans can vote now through the official The Game Awards website .

Six games are competing for the top prize this year. The shortlist mixes new releases, a returning Remedy franchise and Nintendo’s remake of one of the most celebrated games ever made.

Grand Theft Auto VI appears in Game of the Year, Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, Best Score and Music, Best Audio Design, Best Performance, Best Art Direction and Best Action/Adventure Game. The game will not be in players’ hands when voting opens, as millions prepare for GTA 6 launch day streams later this week. Games released on or before 20 November qualified this year, while Players’ Voice entries have until 30 November.

Capcom holds two of the five Best Game Direction slots through Pragmata and Resident Evil Requiem. The Blood of Dawnwalker, the debut game from Rebel Wolves and Bandai Namco, is the only Best Narrative nominee absent from the Game of the Year list. Rahul Kohli earns a Best Performance nomination for Saros, alongside Manni L. Perez for Grand Theft Auto VI.

Big Walk is the most nominated independent release, with four nominations across Games for Impact, Best Independent Game, Best Family Game and Best Multiplayer Game. EA Sports FC 27 and Forza Horizon 6 compete in Best Sports/Racing Game, while Riot Games’ 2XKO features in Best Fighting Game.

title: Is Doki Doki Literature Club (DDLC) coming to Fortnite?
content:
Rumors in the Fortnite community suggest that the popular visual novel game, Doki Doki Literature Club (DDLC), is coming to Fortnite. Many of these leaks have reputable support, with some leakers calling an “80-90%” chance that it will happen.

This article outlines all the details regarding this rumored collab, including when it could drop and what it will feature!

4 UPCOMING ANIME/CEL-SHADED SKINS • All female, each one has a custom lobby pose • At least 2 have cloth physics & 1 has special hair physics • 1 bundle + each skin separately, no other cosmetics MAYBE Doki Doki x Fortnite? (NOTHING CONFIRMED) pic.twitter.com/DnZOd9t4BU

Fortnite leaker HYPEX was among the many to report this rumored collab. However, the initial details cast some doubt on the actual collaboration. HYPEX outlined his theories, explaining that these are anime/cel-shaded skins and that all four are female.

Those details alone have led most leakers down the same path: that DDLC is coming to Fortnite. Another leaker, ShiinaBR, followed with a list of currently encrypted skins , including Doki Doki Literature Club. Shiina added an 80-90% certainty to the post.

Pairing all of the evidence so far with the fact that Epic Games added DDLC to the Epic Games Store in September, there’s little doubt that this will be the rumored collab. It would fit nicely into the current One Piece-inspired season .

title: BGMI Popularity Battle Annual Gala: Registration Dates, Nine Tiers and Rewards
content:
Krafton India is bringing a Popularity Battle Annual Gala to Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI) with the 4.7 update on 18 November. Registration opens on the same day and closes on 24 November. The main event runs from 25 November to 27 December, with a Team Popularity Battle to follow in December. The update also adds a redesigned Mode Selection screen and a seasonal reward event called Chicko’s Loot.

Popularity Battle is BGMI’s social ranking event, in which players compete for recognition within the game’s community. The Annual Gala is a larger version of the format. Krafton India announced the event in Bengaluru on 12 November. It said further ways to earn points will be revealed when the event goes live. It has not said whether the Team Popularity Battle will use the same tiers and rewards.

The Annual Gala has nine ranking tiers. The highest tier is limited to 3,000 players. Each round of the event counts towards a final stage called the Peak Battle, which decides the rewards. Players who reach the top tiers receive exclusive in game honours tied to their ranking. Krafton India has not listed the rewards for each tier.

The event also introduces a Starlight Grand Prize. Every registered player has a chance to win it, regardless of their final tier. Krafton India has not said how many Starlight Grand Prizes will be given out or what the prize includes.

Chicko’s Loot runs from 20 November to 21 January 2027. Players collect Lucky Eggs by playing different game modes or by receiving them as gifts from friends. The eggs can be exchanged for rewards in an event shop. A mini game built around the Lucky Eggs will be added in December.

The Mode Selection screen has been redesigned with two sections, Mine and Discover. Mine lists the modes a player uses most, while Discover shows modes they have not tried. The new screen will reach players in phases during the update rather than all at once.

title: The TenZ Gamble: Why T1’s 2027 Roster Could Struggle
content:
T1’s 2027 VALORANT roster is complete, but three questions hang over it before its first match: who plays which role, which language the team calls in, and whether it can finally win a VCT Pacific league stage. The club confirmed Tyson “TenZ” Ngo on 12 November, ending a retirement that began in September 2024. TenZ replied to the announcement with “I’m back”. Austin “crashies” Roberts had joined a day earlier, and Gustavo “Sacy” Rossi was named head coach on 13 November.

The expected starting five is Kim “stax” Gu-taek, Yu “BuZz” Byung-chul, Ham “iZu” Woo-joo, TenZ and crashies. So “sungmin” Seong-min, previously head coach of T1’s academy side, returns as coach. The team is expected to debut at Red Bull Home Ground in December.

T1 cleared most of its staff on 2 November. Head coach Kim “KDG” Dong-gun and assistant coach Lee “CheongGak” Il-ho left, along with players Meteor, Munchkin and DH. T1 credited KDG with taking the team to its first Champions playoffs. Sacy, a Champions and Masters winner as a player, has never coached a team before. Two new players and a new head coach will start their preparation at the same time.

TenZ built his reputation on duelists, but he moved to controller in his final season with Sentinels. Since retiring, he has played only two professional series, for Sentinels’ academy team in May 2025. stax played controller for T1 in 2026, iZu played initiator and BuZz was the primary duelist. crashies has played both initiator and sentinel.

That leaves two recent controller players for a role most compositions fill once. If TenZ plays controller, stax has to move to another role. If TenZ returns to duelist, he shares the role with BuZz. crashies is the most flexible of the five, and T1 has not said how it will split the roles.

TenZ and crashies are the first non Korean players on T1’s main roster since the team joined VCT Pacific. The squad has three Korean speakers and two English speakers, with a Brazilian head coach. Mixed Pacific teams usually call in English, and crashies has already played in North America and Europe. T1 has not said which language the team will use.

title: LCS : Shopify Rebellion mise sur Massu, Vulcan et Gryffinn
content:
Les choses s’accélèrent du côté de Shopify Rebellion. Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , l’organisation aurait trouvé des accords verbaux avec Fahad « Massu » Abdulmalek et Philippe « Vulcan » Laflamme pour la saison 2027. Les deux Canadiens devraient ainsi former la nouvelle botlane des Rebels, respectivement aux postes d’ADC et de support. Massu aurait notamment été préféré à Tactical et Sushee, tandis que Vulcan aurait été choisi devant Isles. Deux recrues de premier plan pour une équipe déterminée à retrouver les sommets de la scène nord-américaine.

À seulement 21 ans, Massu s’apprêterait à quitter FlyQuest après quatre années passées au sein de l’organisation. Révélé au plus haut niveau en 2024, il avait notamment remporté le titre de Rookie of the Year en LCS avant de briller aux Worlds, où FlyQuest avait poussé Gen.G jusqu’à la cinquième manche en quarts de finale. Malgré deux nouveaux titres régionaux en 2025, sa dernière saison aura été plus compliquée, avec une absence au MSI et aux Worlds 2026. Également courtisé par NAVI et Movistar KOI, le jeune ADC aurait finalement choisi de poursuivre sa carrière en Amérique du Nord.

[SOURCES] Massu is set to join Shopify Rebellion for the 2027 #LCS season After four years with FlyQuest, he will reunite with Quad and form an all-Canadian botlane with Vulcan at SR! Report by @LCS_Eevee , @anonimotum & @LEC_Wooloo https://t.co/ow0bRSlfOF

Pour l’accompagner sur la botlane, Shopify Rebellion miserait sur l’expérience de Vulcan, élu MVP du Spring Split 2026 des LCS. Le support de 27 ans devrait quitter Cloud9 après trois nouvelles saisons sous ses couleurs. Malgré une excellente régularité en saison régulière, C9 n’aura pas réussi à décrocher le moindre titre durant cette période. Son retour aux Worlds en 2026 s’était également soldé par une élimination précoce en Play-In, après deux défaites face à la Karmine Corp et FURIA.

[SOURCES] Vulcan is set to join Shopify Rebellion as starting support for the 2027 LCS season. He will leave Cloud9 after three years with the organization. Report by @LCS_Eevee @anonimotum @LEC_Wooloo https://t.co/PMsu60GDou

Mais le recrutement de Shopify Rebellion ne s’arrêterait pas là. Toujours selon Sheep Esports , Johnson « Gryffinn » Le aurait lui aussi trouvé un accord verbal avec les Rebels. Le jungler américano-vietnamien de 20 ans, arrivé chez FlyQuest en 2026, pourrait ainsi retrouver ses anciens coéquipiers Massu et Quad. Son transfert reste toutefois conditionné à un accord avec FlyQuest, où il est encore sous contrat jusqu’en novembre 2027. L’organisation pourrait même bloquer son départ si elle ne parvient pas à lui trouver un remplaçant.

Travis Scott GTA 6 Air Force 1 Low: Price, Release Date and All Colourways
content:
Travis Scott, Nike and Rockstar Games are releasing a pack of three Air Force 1 Low ’07 sneakers tied to Grand Theft Auto VI. Each pair is expected to cost $130. Release listings first gave 19 November, the day GTA 6 launches, before the date moved to 21 November. Nike and Rockstar have not officially confirmed the price, the date or where the shoes will be sold.

Scott shared the first images of the collaboration on Instagram in early November. He posed with the shoes beside a pink vintage car, with the caption “As a kid it was a game now it’s reality”. Scott also features on GTA VI: The Album with the track “RHYNO”, part of the game’s 34 song soundtrack .

The pack comes in three colourways: white, black, and a black pair covered in multicoloured stars. The star pair carries the style code JJ7603-900 and the colour name Multi Color/Pale Ivory/Black/Bold Berry/Fire Pink. Images of all three leaked in the first week of November, before Scott confirmed the project himself.

Each shoe swaps the usual “AIR” lettering on the midsole for “GTA”. The designs also carry Scott’s reverse Swoosh, a feature of his earlier Nike collaborations. The star pattern refers to the wanted level system used across the GTA series, and the black pair shows a full six star wanted level.

Nike has not published a product page or said which apps and stores will carry the pack. Nike has sold earlier Travis Scott collaborations through its SNKRS app, Scott’s Cactus Jack website and selected retailers. Those releases usually sold out quickly and appeared on resale sites at higher prices within hours.

title: LCK : Cuzz quitte KT Rolster pour retrouver DN SOOPers
content:

Selon les informations de Sheep Esports , le jungler sud-coréen devrait quitter KT Rolster pour rejoindre DN SOOPers lors de la saison 2027 de LCK. Un retour aux sources pour le vétéran de 26 ans, qui avait déjà porté les couleurs de l’organisation en 2024, lorsqu’elle évoluait encore sous le nom de Freecs. Présent au plus haut niveau depuis 2017, Cuzz possède une solide expérience de la scène coréenne. Malgré les difficultés de DN SOOPers en championnat, Sharvel a montré de belles promesses depuis son arrivée. title: GTA 6’s Leonida’s Weather Teases Six New Screenshots, Shows How Wild Its Weather Gets
content:
The Weather Channel spent Monday afternoon, US time, forecasting a state that does not exist. Three days before Grand Theft Auto VI launches on 19 November, the American TV network posted a six-part forecast for Leonida, the fictional version of Florida where the game is set. Each post came with a new screenshot supplied by Rockstar Games, and the opening post had passed 5.2 million views on X by Tuesday evening in India.

Nobody knows weather like we do. That’s why @rockstargames gave us an exclusive look at the forecast for Leonida and the dynamic weather in GTAVI. “Grand Theft Auto VI takes place in Leonida – a fictional world inspired by modern-day Florida, a landscape with one of the most…

The partnership is a marketing stunt, but the choice of subject is deliberate. Weather has been one of the systems Rockstar has talked about most in the run-up to launch, and the thread came with a statement from Owen Shepherd, Rockstar’s VP of Art for Light and Rendering. “We had to completely reimagine our in-game weather systems to feel more localized, persistent, and above all dynamic,” he said, describing skies that range “from clear blue skies to towering vertiginous cumulonimbus clouds”.

Shepherd also explained why Leonida needed that work in the first place. He called it “a fictional world inspired by modern-day Florida, a landscape with one of the most unpredictable weather systems in the US”. That makes it worth looking at the six forecasts closely, both for what they show about the game and for how they compare with the real Florida.

The forecasts are written in The Weather Channel’s familiar on-air voice, but every detail points back to the game. The first warns that heavy rain is making visibility poor across “many places in the Keys”, and adds that local authorities have installed reflectors on some roads. It finishes with a joke about getting your headlights fixed at Coastal Auto Care, which appears to be one of Leonida’s in-game businesses.

The second forecast moves inland, to the swamps of Pelican Valley. “The water is murky at the best of times but this storm’s made it nearly impossible to spot the big nibblers,” the post reads. That line is a nod to the alligators Rockstar has already confirmed among the animals of Leonida , and the screenshot shows a storm front rolling across flooded grassland.

title: JioBLAST’s First VCT Qualifier Opens With Self-Hosted Matches and a Last-Minute Bracket Change
content:
The VCT 2027 Kickoff Open Qualifiers for South Asia began on 17 November, and the first day of JioBLAST’s first Valorant Champions Tour event drew complaints from players before many of the opening matches had finished. Teams said they were left to set up their own match lobbies, and one player said a new schedule and bracket arrived on Discord an hour before his team was due to play. JioBLAST , the Indian venture that pairs Jio with BLAST, had not commented publicly on the complaints by the evening.

What you said here is one thing, and there’s one more thing I’d like to add. Since I’m also playing in this VCT Qualifier, I honestly can’t get my head around the fact that the admins/management released the schedule and match timings last night, around 11 PM–12 AM on the 16th… https://t.co/LwX4ivTRe6

Riot Games named JioBLAST as the organiser in early November, after NODWIN Gaming ran South Asia’s Challengers circuit in 2026. As our guide to the South Asia Open Qualifiers explained, the Swiss stage runs from 17 to 20 November and sends eight teams to a double-elimination playoff from 23 to 29 November. Only two teams will go on to Kickoff APAC, and the playoffs will be broadcast.

The loudest complaint came from a post by an Indian esports news account on X, published at 1:25 pm Indian time, shortly before the first matches were due to start. It said there were “no mods, no admins” to oversee the opening matches, and that teams had been asked to contact each other, set up their games and play. By the evening, the post had passed 25,000 views, far more than JioBLAST’s own post announcing the qualifier the day before.

A more detailed account came from inside the event. Hassan Aseel “Asitte” Rasheed, a Maldivian player who was named Best Esports PC Player of the Year at awards backed by Ooredoo Maldives in 2023, said he was playing in the qualifier himself. In his post on X , he said the schedule and match timings were released at around 11 pm to midnight on 16 November, with matches due to start from 2 pm Indian time the next day.

“That was fine, even though it wasn’t a full 24 hours’ notice,” Rasheed wrote. On 17 November, however, he said teams were told on Discord, an hour before their scheduled matches, that a new schedule and new brackets had been released. “It now seems like we have to play a BO3 today,” he added, and said many teams were raising the same issue in Discord voice chats and channels.

title: Nvidia Board Creates National Security Committee as Washington Presses for Answers on China Chips
content:
Nvidia’s board has set up a new committee to watch over the company’s national security work and export controls, five days after Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive. The National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee was announced on 17 November, the same day Nvidia reports its third-quarter results, the first under interim chief executive Colette Kress. In its announcement , Nvidia said the new standing committee will be responsible for board-level oversight of “national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management”.

The NVIDIA Board of Directors has established the National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee. Read the release: https://t.co/uIeCqHURiI

The timing is hard to separate from the pressure building in Washington. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has demanded answers from Nvidia’s board within 10 days, as we reported when he called for a “dramatic shakeup” at the company. A day before the committee was announced, the Commerce and Justice departments said in a rare joint statement that they had been investigating the Singapore cloud company Megaspeed since 2024.

Director Suzanne Nora Johnson, a former vice chairman of Goldman Sachs, will chair the committee. The other two members are Stephen Neal, chairman emeritus and senior counsel at the law firm Cooley, and John O. Dabiri, a professor of aeronautics and mechanical engineering at Caltech. All three are listed on Nvidia’s board of directors page , which now names Harvey Jones as chair.

Judging by those biographies, none of the three comes from a national security or export control background. The board appears to know it, because the committee will hire “independent, outside experts” in law, national security and trade compliance to support its work. It will meet at least four times a year, including sessions with management and private sessions without them.

The change to reporting lines may matter more than the committee itself. Nvidia’s existing National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team will now report directly to the committee, as well as to Kress on day-to-day operations. That gives the board a direct line to the teams that handle export compliance, rather than hearing from them only through management.

title: Legacy CS2 Orgs Could Quit If They Miss Majors, Warns TechGirl, as Sticker Money Dries Up
content:
Counter-Strike’s biggest names could start walking away from the game if they keep missing Majors, according to presenter and podcaster Sam “TechGirl” Wright. Speaking on the latest episode of Feed the Trolls , her show with Duncan “Thorin” Shields, she said she thinks “a lot of these legacy orgs eventually pull out of Counter-Strike if they’re not making the Major”. The warning lands a week before the PGL Major Singapore begins on 24 November, with fnatic, NRG, paiN and TYLOO all missing from the 32-team field.

Wright’s point is about money as much as prestige. Since Valve rebuilt the Major sticker system in May, an organisation’s income from the biggest event of the season depends far more on how far it goes. Teams that do not qualify get nothing at all, and for clubs with large wage bills and few other reliable revenue streams, that gap is getting harder to absorb.

For years, Major stickers were sold in capsules, and organisations and players negotiated their own splits in their contracts. Valve scrapped capsules for the IEM Cologne Major in May 2026 and moved to a Major Shop, where fans buy the exact stickers they want with tokens. Half of all sales still go to the tournament organiser, the teams and the players. What changed is that Valve now sets each team’s royalty rate by its seeding before the Major and its final placing after it, as Counter-Strike’s official account announced at the time.

The gap between the top and bottom of that scale is wide. The Major champion receives 2.85% of token sales, while the bottom-placed teams receive 0.72%, and each team’s share is now split evenly between the organisation and its five players. On every $100 million of sales, that leaves a champion’s organisation with about $1.43 million and a first-stage casualty’s with about $360,000. At Cologne, the bottom rate went to Gaimin Gladiators and SINNERS, whose organisations each took just 0.36%.

Some team owners warned about this months ago. M80 chief executive Marco Mereu said in June that the change “could cause teams to refocus on other events besides the Majors” as they look for income. Reports since then have described sales slowing sharply after the Cologne launch, and Valve skipped its usual end-of-event sticker sale for the first time. For organisations that relied on a healthy sticker cheque even after an early exit, the budget maths has changed, and missing the Major altogether now leaves an even bigger gap against rivals who go deep.

Wright also took aim at one organiser in particular. On the podcast, she said that “apparently” the chief executive of FiReSPORTS had claimed the sticker situation would be fixed after Singapore. “How convenient that leads into his Majors,” she added. FiReSPORTS , the Argentine company behind FiReLEAGUE, will host the first Major of 2027 in Buenos Aires, before Perfect World stages the second in Shanghai.

title: IEM Beijing locked in through 2028 as EFG signs 3-year deal with city esports body
content:
Under a three-year framework deal that ESL FACEIT Group (EFG) concluded with the Beijing Esports Industry Development Association, Intel Extreme Masters (IEM) Beijing will be held each year as a Counter-Strike 2 (CS2) tournament between 2026 and 2028. The deal was rubber stamped at a ceremony during IEM Beijing 2026, Insider Gaming detailed.

The Bloomage Biotech Biohyalux ECM Arena in Wukesong, Haidian District, successfully hosted IEM Beijing 2026 earlier this month, which MOUZ won. The Association, which is supervised by the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Press and Publication, will now start working closely with EFG and local authorities on a long-term support structure. The aim is for broadcasters, sponsors, and Chinese esports clubs to get the commercial safety net they crave.

Marc Winther, Director of Esports Counter-Strike 2 at EFG, hailed the deal as a flagship event for domestic fans. He also said the arrangement offers teams and partners in the area a stable footing for expansion.

Looking at the figures, it’s no surprise that EFG wanted to hang around: the 2026 edition prompted almost 60,000 fans to turn up across six days of competition, which EFG calls the biggest standalone IEM held in Asia ever . It also revived IEM's 360-degree arena stage for the first time since 2022, when the IEM Rio Major took place.

The commitment follows a run of strong domestic numbers. IEM's standalone Chinese debut was in Beijing in 2019. IEM Chengdu in 2025 sold out with more than 35,000 attendees and 770,000 peak online viewers. Research firm Niko Partners estimates CS2 pulled 137.5 million viewers on Chinese livestreaming platforms in June 2026, up 50 percent month on month, making it the second most-watched shooter in the territory.

title: LCK : T1 prépare le grand retour de Roach

Âgé de 27 ans, l’ancien toplaner retrouverait ainsi une organisation dont il a porté les couleurs pendant cinq ans, entre 2020 et 2024, avant de s’éloigner de la compétition pour effectuer son service militaire.

Arrivé chez T1 comme joueur en 2020, Roach avait progressivement entamé sa reconversion sur le banc. Après une première expérience avec l’équipe académique en 2022, il avait intégré le staff de l’équipe première à l’été 2023. Il avait notamment participé aux deux sacres consécutifs de T1 aux Worlds 2023 et 2024, ainsi qu’à la victoire lors de la première édition de l’Esports World Cup en 2024. title: AnkiiiBot Defends Aadi Over Team SouL Targeting Controversy
content:
Nebula Esports, led by former IGL Aditya “Aadi” Dawar, targeted Team SouL in the last match of Battlegrounds Mobile India Showdown 2026 (BMSD 2026). Although he explained his reason behind his actions , the criticism did not seem to stop. BGMI caster Ankit “AnkiiiBOT” Pandey recently shared his two cents on the controversy.

In a recent livestream, in the context of Nebula Esports (former roster) targeting Team SouL, AnkiiiBot asserted that there’s nothing wrong with it and that it is a part of the game. “I don’t know, man. Why do people take this stuff so personally? Targeting and all is part of the game, period.”

Further clarifying his stance, AnkiiiBot added that Aadi doesn’t need to explain why he targeted someone. “It’s a game. You felt like doing it, you did it.”

He staunchly added that there is no official rule against targeting another team, and if someone has a problem, they can get a rule written down by Krafton itself saying that you can’t target. However, he was quick to clarify that he was not isolating this event, but he is talking about all the ‘targeting’ controversies that have emerged over the past few years. “I’m not saying this just about this particular matter. There have been plenty of instances like this, whether it was regarding Hector or some other team.”

AnkiiiBot recalled a similar instance that happened with RevenantXSpark and GodLike Esports in BGMI Pro Series 2026 (BMPS 2026) and Battlegrounds Mobile India Series (BGIS 2026). He asserted that it is a sensible thing to do against a strong team because naturally they would want to eliminate the strongest competition from the lobby. “ Why wouldn’t they? You’re a strong team. They would want you out of the tournament. They wouldn’t want you to win a trophy.” He added, “So what’s the big deal? In the next tournament (BMPS 2026), you targeted them, you even won , and that was that. The tournament was settled.”

Sharing his personal opinion, AnkiiiBot said, “Everyone should just do whatever they want.”

title: Aadi Reveals Why He Targeted Team SouL in BMSD 2026, Alleges Poaching
content:
Vasista Esports’ current BGMI IGL Aditya “Aadi” Dawar explained why he targeted Team SouL in the final match of BGMI Showdown 2026 (BMSD 2026), while he was playing for Nebula Esports. He also revisited the poaching incidents he has faced throughout his career since Team SouL signed Goblin from iNSANE Esports in 2022.

Over the years, as the IGL, he has fostered multiple esports athletes who have been making waves in the esports scene or have won multiple official esports events. When Aadi recently went live on his YouTube channel, his viewers started spamming why Nebula Esports, his erstwhile team in BMSD 2026, targeted Team SouL in the last match on Miramar. Maybe Krafton gave these guys special permission, or I honestly don’t know, because how can you change a player during the lock-in window? Perhaps Krafton gave them permission to make changes even during the lock-in period. I have no idea,” he sarcastically added.

Aadi went on to question Team SouL’s intention behind the call. “What really got to me was if you can’t actually sign the player, why are you calling him in the first place? Since the start of his career, Aadi has fostered a lot of underdog players and made them a few of the finest in the esports scene. title: PS5 Hacker Gezine Claims Game Dump on Firmware 14.22, the Version GTA 6 Reportedly Needs
content:
PlayStation 5 security researcher Gezine has claimed to have dumped a game executable on PS5 system software 14.22. Grand Theft Auto VI reportedly needs that firmware version to run, and the game launches on 19 November. Gezine announced the result on X but did not name the game. He has not shared his method, published any files or released a tool.

A game executable, also called a game binary, is the program code a game needs to run. The PS5 keeps that code encrypted and protected. Dumping it means copying the code out of the console in a readable form. It is one step in examining how a game works, but it does not amount to a full jailbreak of the console.

Gezine had previously said the established method for dumping games stopped working on firmware 14.00 and later. On 19 October he posted that the “old way to dump executables does not seem to work at 14.xx”. He suggested at the time that a hypervisor exploit might be needed. The new claim suggests he has found another route, although he has not explained it.

In late October, Gezine also shared screenshots that appeared to show access to the debug menu on firmware 14.10. Sony released firmware 14.22 on 2 November. Public exploit tools still stop at firmware 13.60, and no public jailbreak exists for any 14.xx version. On 13 November, another modder, Echo Stretch, warned players not to expect a pirated copy of GTA 6.

A dumped executable is also what emulator developers and modders study when they try to run console games on other hardware. Even so, a single dump on one console does not let other players copy or run games. Running a dumped game on a PS5 would still need a working jailbreak on the same firmware, and none has been shown for 14.22. Gezine has not said whether he plans to go further.

Gezine is known in the console homebrew scene for keeping his findings to himself. He reports vulnerabilities to companies through bug bounty programmes instead of releasing them publicly. He has found security flaws in both Nintendo and PlayStation consoles. That approach means a public tool based on this work may never appear.

title: OpTic Gaming est de retour en LCS
content:
Après sept années d’absence, OpTic Gaming va retrouver l’élite nord-américaine de League of Legends. L’organisation américaine, aujourd’hui principalement présente sur Call of Duty, prendra la place de Dignitas pour la saison 2027 des LCS. Un retour particulièrement attendu pour une structure historique de l’esport, qui compte parmi les communautés de supporters les plus fidèles d’Amérique du Nord.

OpTic avait déjà tenté l’aventure sur League of Legends entre 2018 et 2019, sans parvenir à s’imposer parmi les meilleures équipes du championnat. Son meilleur résultat reste une cinquième place lors du Summer Split 2019, avec notamment le champion du monde 2017 Crown dans ses rangs. L’organisation avait également accueilli Romain Bigeard, aujourd’hui directeur général de G2 Esports, avant de quitter la ligue à la suite de son rachat par Immortals. Son fondateur, Hector « H3CZ » Rodriguez, avait finalement récupéré OpTic en novembre 2020.

Ce retour marque également la fin d’une époque pour Dignitas, l’une des organisations historiques de la scène nord-américaine. Présente en LCS dès 2013, puis revenue en 2020 après deux années d’absence, la structure n’a jamais réussi à décrocher le moindre titre dans la compétition. Malgré plusieurs qualifications pour les playoffs, elle n’a pas non plus disputé de finale ni participé à un tournoi international.

Avec OpTic Gaming, les LCS récupèrent donc une marque emblématique de l’esport nord-américain. Reste désormais à découvrir les ambitions sportives du Green Wall et les joueurs qui composeront son effectif pour 2027. Une chose est sûre : le retour d’OpTic promet d’apporter un nouvel engouement autour du championnat.

title: BGMI Joins Google Play Arena: Free Registration, MS Dhoni’s Mahi Clutchers and a Mumbai LAN Finale
content:
Krafton India has added Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI) and Real Cricket to Google Play Arena, the club-based mobile gaming championship run by Google Play with NODWIN Gaming. BGMI’s open qualifiers are already under way. Registration is free, open to players aged 18 and above, and closes on 27 November. The championship ends with a ticketed LAN finale in Mumbai on 19 and 20 December.

Top performers from the qualifiers will represent one of six clubs at the finale. The clubs are Team S8UL, GodLike Esports, Orangutan Gaming, Revenant XSpark, Team Apex Gaming and Mahi Clutchers. Mahi Clutchers is a new club led by former India cricket captain MS Dhoni. Its roster will be built entirely through the open qualifiers.

Both tracks meet at the Mumbai finale, where the championship will be decided in front of a live audience.

Google Play Arena has no entry fee and no paid entry routes. Players qualify on results alone. The full schedule is published on the Google Play Arena page. Organisers have not disclosed the prize pool, the Mumbai venue or ticket prices for the finale.

BGMI covers the shooter category in the championship, while Real Cricket brings in a cricket title. Krafton India has not yet given dates or a format for the Real Cricket competition. The organisers have also not said which other games are part of Google Play Arena.

title: Paper Rex’s something Reportedly Cleared as a Pacific Resident, Freeing an Import Slot
content:
Paper Rex may have found the roster loophole every VCT Pacific team wanted. Riot Games has granted Ilia “something” Petrov an exception that lets him count as a Pacific resident in 2027, according to a report by Lion Esports on 16 November. The Russian duelist joined the Singapore club from Japan’s Sengoku Gaming in March 2023. If that holds, something would no longer take up one of Paper Rex’s two import slots, and the club could add a foreign player without breaking up its core. Riot and Paper Rex have not confirmed the ruling, although the club’s X account did little to cool the speculation the next morning.

Robert Pattinson to play under PRX for VCT 2027 pic.twitter.com/p19yPGsqWu

Lion Esports, citing sources close to the matter, said the decision also covers other long-serving Russian players in the region, naming Maksim “Jemkin” Batorov. It added that Riot had not said publicly what threshold it used, whether that was years of residency, years under contract in Asia or a case-by-case review. That gap matters, because the 2027 rules give Riot wide discretion here, and the timing comes weeks after Paper Rex lost Jinggg and d4v41.

The answer sits in Riot’s VCT Global Policies for 2027 , last updated on 28 September. Article 96 says a player can count as a resident of a region if they are a citizen, a lawful permanent resident or hold another special status such as refugee status. The fourth route is the one that matters here, because it covers a player who “was granted an exception to be considered a Resident”, which Riot may accept or reject at its discretion. There is no fixed number of years in the rulebook, so a case like something’s depends entirely on Riot’s judgement.

Article 108 then sets the hard limit on imports. Every team must field at least three residents of its home region in its starting five, which means a maximum of two non-residents. Articles 109 to 112 add a softer route for teams that kept their partnership, such as Paper Rex. These legacy exceptions let a starting lineup carry more than two non-residents, but only if every one of those players holds an exception, and each one ends when that player’s contract with the club expires.

That is why a residency exception is worth far more than a legacy one. A legacy exception protects a player only for the length of his deal and only alongside other protected players. A residency exception, if Riot has granted it, removes something from the import count altogether, so Paper Rex could sign two new non-residents around him instead of none.

title: Microsoft’s 24-Hour Outage Cost Customers About $9 Billion. Microsoft Pays a Fraction
content:
For almost 24 hours last week, much of the working world could not open its email. Microsoft’s preliminary incident report puts the Microsoft 365 outage at 23 hours and 50 minutes, from 16:20 UTC on 12 November to 16:10 UTC the next day, with Outlook and Exchange Online hit hardest. By TalkEsport’s estimate, it cost Microsoft’s customers around the world about $9 billion in lost working time, within a plausible range of $2 billion to $27 billion. Microsoft’s own maximum exposure, through the service credits it promises when it misses its uptime target, is less than a billion dollars, and its share price rose on both days of the outage.

That gap is the real story of the outage. The failure was Microsoft’s, the evidence in its own report suggests it was preventable, and yet nearly all of the cost landed on the companies, hospitals, schools and governments that pay for Microsoft 365. We built a simple model to put a number on it, and every step is shown below so readers can swap in any assumption they disagree with.

Microsoft has been unusually candid about the cause. Its preliminary post-incident report , dated 15 November and shared with administrators under incident IDs EX1550543 and MO1550821, describes a fix it built for the networking gateway that sits in front of many Microsoft 365 services. That fix carried a hidden defect, and it went live across the world from July onwards. For more than three months, it ran without causing any visible problem.

The defect was lock contention inside an internal Windows process, which meant tasks on the gateway servers waited on each other until processor time and memory ran out. Microsoft’s report admits that its load tests “tended to focus on weaker hardware with fewer cores”, while the bug got worse on newer machines with more cores. On 12 November, a routine Teams failover added load to the same gateway, nearly 14% of its capacity was already offline for an unrelated reason, and US peak traffic did the rest. As we reported while Outlook and Teams were still down , Microsoft spent most of the first night restarting servers that kept failing again.

The report’s own words explain why this one lasted so long. Automated traffic management moved users to healthy servers, which then hit the same bug, and “at its lowest, more than 80% of servers were unresponsive”. Because the faulty change was months old, Microsoft said its “normal rollback, flighting, and feature flags were unable to quickly revert the change”. Engineers had to build a new update instead, and it did not reach the first servers until 07:20 UTC on 13 November, 15 hours after the outage began.

While we're working to mitigate impact, we've confirmed the issue may affect Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region, more information will be provided in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543.

title: US Breaks Silence on Megaspeed: Probe Began in 2024, Nvidia Cut It Off in June 2025
content:
The US government has broken its silence on Megaspeed, and its account puts Nvidia’s own role in a new light. In a rare joint statement dated 16 November, the Department of Commerce and the Department of Justice said they had been investigating the Singapore company since 2024. They also said Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its “no sell” list in June 2025, after Commerce investigators asked the chipmaker for records of its sales. The criminal case is now led by the Justice Department, and the two agencies promised to bring “the full extent of the law” against Megaspeed for any crimes it may have committed.

The agencies said they were speaking because of “inaccurate information circulating in public reporting”, although they did not say which reports they meant. Megaspeed is the cloud company whose former chief executive, Alice Huang, is at the centre of the scandal that ended Jensen Huang’s 33 years as Nvidia’s chief executive on 12 November. No charges against Megaspeed or Alice Huang have been announced, and Megaspeed has denied diverting Nvidia chips to China.

The statement sets out the clearest official timeline yet. According to the two departments, Commerce opened its investigation in 2024 “after identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring” of possible chip diversion. In May 2025, its investigators asked Nvidia for records of any direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed, and in June 2025 Nvidia added Megaspeed to its “no sell” list. That same month, agents from the Bureau of Industry and Security carried out an on-site end-use check at Megaspeed with Singaporean law enforcement officers. They also interviewed Alice Huang, whom the statement describes as the company’s chief executive.

An end-use check is one of the US government’s main tools for confirming that exported technology is where its buyer says it is, and is being used for the purpose declared. Doing one in person, alongside another country’s police, is a sign that investigators were already treating the case seriously by mid-2025. According to the statement, it was only “following this enforcement action” that the Justice Department took the lead in a criminal investigation, with Commerce’s export enforcement agents still working the case alongside federal prosecutors.

The statement also doubles as a defence of the government’s record. It credits Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, whom Senator Tom Cotton had urged to investigate Megaspeed , and Attorney General Todd Blanche. It also says 17 defendants in six separate investigations have been charged under the Trump administration over alleged smuggling of semiconductors worth billions of dollars. Commerce adds that its export control penalties are now 18 times higher than under the Biden administration. One of those prosecutions is a Southern District of New York case against three people accused of diverting US AI technology to China.

The timing makes the target of the statement fairly clear. On 9 November, The New York Times reported that the Commerce investigation was handed to the Justice Department after Nvidia’s general counsel, Tim Teter, contacted investigators in August 2025. The Times said Teter told investigators that Jeffrey Kessler, the Commerce under secretary who oversees export controls, had given him permission to reach out. Some agents reportedly worried that the contact could taint the case, and the Times said Commerce paused its own work at the Justice Department’s request.

title: LEC 2027 : date de reprise, format, Roadtrips… ce qu’il faut savoir
content:
Le compte à rebours est lancé pour le championnat européen de League of Legends. La saison 2027 du LEC débutera officiellement le vendredi 15 janvier, avec le coup d’envoi du Winter Split. Riot Games a confirmé le maintien des trois segments traditionnels (Winter, Spring et Summer), sans bouleversement majeur du format. L’éditeur souhaite ainsi poursuivre sur la lancée de la saison précédente, en conservant une formule qui a fait ses preuves.

Comme lors des segments de printemps et d’été 2026, les dix équipes s’affronteront en Bo3 lors de la saison régulière, dans un format où chaque formation rencontrera une fois ses neuf adversaires. Les six meilleures équipes se qualifieront ensuite pour les playoffs, intégralement disputés en Bo5. La Fearless Draft et le système de Sélection prioritaire seront également conservés tout au long de l’année. Une chose est sûre : aucun match en Bo1 ne sera au programme de cette saison 2027.

LEC RETURNS ON JANUARY 15 Winter, Spring and Summer: Check out the (old) new format for all three splits! pic.twitter.com/ig6FaCDwVC

L’autre grande annonce concerne les LEC Roadtrips, qui feront leur retour pour une troisième année consécutive. Après cinq événements délocalisés organisés en partenariat avec la Karmine Corp et Movistar KOI en 2026, Riot Games souhaite poursuivre le développement de cette initiative. L’objectif sera de collaborer avec davantage d’organisations pour faire voyager le championnat dans de nouvelles villes à travers la région EMEA.

Une excellente nouvelle pour les supporters européens, qui avaient notamment pu assister à des rencontres à Barcelone, Madrid, Évry, Paris ou encore Nice cette année. Les nouvelles destinations restent toutefois à déterminer, tout comme le calendrier détaillé du Winter Split. Riot Games promet de communiquer davantage d’informations dans les prochaines semaines, avant une reprise qui s’annonce particulièrement attendue après un mercato mouvementé.

title: LEC 2027 Drops Best-of-One Matches as Riot Confirms Major Format Changes
content:
Riot Games has officially revealed its plans for the League of Legends EMEA Championship (LEC) in 2027, confirming that best-of-one matches will disappear entirely from the competition. All three splits will feature best-of-three regular-season matches and best-of-five playoff series, creating a consistent competitive structure throughout the year.

The announcement, published on November 16, also confirms that the Winter Split begins on January 15, 2027. Riot intends to maintain familiar competitive mechanics while expanding its popular Roadtrip events across Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

The biggest change concerns the structure of the Winter, Spring and Summer Splits.

Unlike 2026, when the opening competition used a different format, all three splits in 2027 will follow the same structure.

Ten teams will compete in a single round-robin regular season, facing every opponent once in a best-of-three series.

The six highest-ranked teams will advance to the playoffs, where every matchup will be decided through a best-of-five series.

title: GTA 6 Has Already Made $1.5 Billion, and Nobody Has Played It Yet
content:
GTA 6 is not out yet, and it has already pulled in about $1.5 billion. Sensor Tower's tracker counts close to 15 million pre-orders on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S with three days to go.

Sensor Tower's live tracker now shows $1.45 billion in revenue and 14.94 million copies sold for GTA 6 as of November 16. That covers PS5 and Xbox Series X|S only, across the Standard and Ultimate Editions. Round it up and you get 15 million copies and roughly $1.5 billion, with the game not out until November 19.

These are estimates. Rockstar and Take-Two have not published a pre-order total, and tracker figures can miss sales or count some twice, so treat the exact numbers with care.

The jump is the real story. When we last checked the tracker , it counted 9.69 million pre-orders and about $942 million. Since then it has added around 5.25 million copies and roughly $508 million. That is about a million extra copies every day.

Our own math on the new totals gives about $97 per copy. The base game lists at $79.99 on Amazon, so a lot of that money is likely coming from buyers who picked the pricier Ultimate Edition.

The latest split is 74% PS5 and 26% Xbox Series X|S. PlayStation alone has brought in just over a billion dollars. Xbox is holding a bigger share than many expected, and it has crept up a point since our last report.

title: Petition to Reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO Passes 175,000 Signatures
content:
An online petition calling on Nvidia’s board to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive has passed 175,000 signatures. About 8,800 of the signatories say they work at Nvidia, a figure that has not been independently verified. The campaign, called “Stand With Jensen”, later showed more than 178,000 names on 16 November. Nvidia has not commented on the petition, and its site states that neither Nvidia nor Huang endorses it.

The petition takes the form of an open letter to Nvidia’s board. It asks the board to reinstate Huang while an independent investigation establishes the facts, to give him a fair hearing and to explain its decision publicly. Huang resigned on 12 November after admitting to an extramarital relationship, ending 33 years as chief executive . Chief financial officer Colette Kress became interim chief executive.

Huang’s resignation followed weeks of scrutiny over his personal relationships. He admitted to being unfaithful to his wife, Lori Huang, in a letter to staff on 8 November. Questions had already been raised about his meetings with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore data centre company Megaspeed. Two sources later said he had a relationship with a second Nvidia employee , a claim Nvidia declined to address. The board opened an independent investigation, which is still under way.

Tesla and SpaceX chief executive Elon Musk said on X on 13 November that he was signing the petition. Epic Games chief executive Tim Sweeney, Replit chief executive Amjad Masad, Uber cofounder Travis Kalanick and Shopify chief executive Tobias Lütke are also listed among the signatories. Musk had earlier said that hiring Huang “would be an honour” .

Not every name on the list is genuine. Some people listed as signatories said they never signed it. The organisers said on X that they were “actively working” to remove fake signatures. They have not said how they verify that a signatory works at Nvidia, and the 8,800 figure relies on what each person entered when signing.

The petition grew quickly over the weekend after Huang stepped down. It passed 100,000 signatures within days of going live. The campaign site counter showed 135,468 signatures on 15 November, before the total moved past 175,000 the following day. The organisers have not said who set up the campaign or whether they plan to deliver the letter to Nvidia’s board in person.

title: How Long Is GTA 6? New Estimate Puts the Main Story Below Rockstar’s 80 Hours
content:
A new estimate of how long Grand Theft Auto VI takes to finish emerged days before its 19 November launch, and it is shorter than the figure many players expected. The estimate covers the main story, the number of missions and the time needed to unlock every trophy. A person with knowledge of the game gave the figures. Rockstar Games has not confirmed them, and it has not published an official completion time.

Until now, the only number in circulation came from Rockstar itself. Studio head Rob Nelson said his own playthrough took about 80 hours. That figure spread online as the length of the main story. Nelson said, however, that his run also covered “optional goals with narrative ramifications”, side tasks whose outcomes affect the story.

The main story of GTA 6 takes about 50 hours to complete. The campaign is said to contain nearly 100 missions spread across five chapters. The estimate covers the main missions featuring Jason and Lucia, the game’s two lead characters. It does not include side activities, optional missions or time spent exploring the state of Leonida.

Unlocking every trophy or achievement is expected to take 200 hours or more. Playtime will also vary with how quickly each player moves through missions. Rockstar has not said how many missions the game contains or how the story is divided. The full list of GTA 6 trophies appeared before launch , giving players an early view of what a full completion requires.

The two figures are not in conflict. A player who follows only the main missions would finish in less time than Nelson, while one who also completes the optional story goals would take closer to his 80 hours. A full completion run, covering every activity and collectible, would take longer than both. Rockstar has not said how much optional content the game holds.

A 50 hour campaign would make GTA 6 the longest main story in the series. Player data on the HowLongToBeat website puts the main story of GTA 5 at about 32 hours. Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar’s last major release in 2018, takes about 50 hours for its main story on the same site. GTA 6 would therefore sit close to Red Dead Redemption 2 rather than GTA 5.

title: GTA 6 Boxed Copy Codes Can Be Read Through Sealed Cases, Buyers Say
content:
Buyers say the download code inside some boxed copies of Grand Theft Auto VI can be read without opening the box. A video posted on X on 13 November showed a person shining a bright torch through the side of a sealed case at an angle. The full redeem code became visible through the cover. Rockstar Games has not commented on the claims, and it has not said how many copies could be affected.

The boxed edition of GTA 6 contains no disc, only a code for the PlayStation Store or the Microsoft Store. In the affected copies, the code is printed directly on the inside of the cover. Rockstar did not use a separate paper insert or a scratch panel to hide it. Anyone who reads the code from a sealed box on a shop shelf could redeem it before the buyer does.

Buyers on the ResetEra forum said the issue appears limited to copies sold in regions that use the PEGI age rating system. Copies sold in the US carry a printed backing behind the code that hides it from the outside. Some testers were unable to repeat the trick with their own boxes. That suggests the problem may depend on the region or the print run, although this has not been confirmed.

There have been no confirmed cases of codes being stolen this way. The claims came a few days after other buyers said their boxes arrived with no code at all, or with a code that had already been redeemed . Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two Interactive has said whether the two issues are linked. Sony’s GTA VI code support page tells buyers with a damaged or missing code to “contact the retailer for help”.

Rockstar chose to ship the boxed edition of GTA 6 with a code instead of a game disc. The company has not explained the decision in detail. Earlier leaks of footage and trailers had raised concerns that boxed copies sold early by retailers could spread story details before launch. A code also means the box itself holds no part of the game, so a buyer cannot install anything until the code is redeemed online.

The format has drawn complaints from collectors and from players with slow internet connections. The game requires a large download before it can be played, and the box offers no way to install it offline. Buyers in Japan have also found that codes in boxed copies there carry a 170 day expiry date. Rockstar has not said whether the same limit applies in other regions.

title: The CS2 Mayonnaise Team: How Hellmann’s Became FURIA’s Most Famous Sponsor
content:

mayonnaise team just 3-0’d spirit lmao https://t.co/4WSOR8Udus

The partnership is a lot older than the meme, though. Hellmann’s , the Unilever mayonnaise brand that started in a New York deli in 1913, signed with FURIA in August 2024 and put its logo on the club’s uniforms. The two sides renewed the partnership in March 2026 with a fan promotion built around IEM Rio. FURIA’s run to the BLAST Rivals Season 2 title simply put the logo in front of more people than ever.

Hellmann’s first worked with FURIA at Casa FURIA, the club’s fan event, in 2022, before signing a full partnership in August 2024. That deal covered the logo on FURIA’s uniforms, joint content and activations around events such as IEM Cologne, CBLOL and the Esports World Cup, according to MKT Esportivo. André Akkari, FURIA’s co-founder and co-CEO, said at the time that the partnership “not only validates our organisation as the leader in Latin America in the sector”.

For Hellmann’s, the reason was the size and age of FURIA’s audience. Unilever told Máquina do Esporte in September 2024 that Hellmann’s wanted to rejuvenate and widen its consumer base. The same plan took in NBA-themed sauce squeezes in Brazil and deals as the official sauce brand at the Allianz Parque and Mineirão football stadiums. “We made a very conscious choice with the NBA and FURIA, which have very large and loyal fan bases,” said Carolina Riotto, then Unilever’s food marketing director.

The mayonnaise jokes leave out part of the picture. FURIA signed a two-year deal with the bookmaker BetBoom on 2 October 2025, which put the BetBoom logo on its CS2 jersey and made FalleN a brand ambassador. The club has also partnered with PokerStars in the past, and Akkari is himself a professional poker player. Hellmann’s sits on the same shirt as betting money, rather than in place of it.

title: Two Time PMGC MVP TOP Backs ScoutOP During Bigg Boss 20 Run
content:
Two-time PUBG Mobile Global Championship (PMGC) MVP Burenbayar “TOP” Altangerel has publicly backed Tanmay “ScoutOP” Singh during his run on Bigg Boss 20. The Mongolian player commented “scoutOP” with three fire emojis under a reel on ScoutOP’s Instagram account. The comment, posted from TOP’s account , had drawn 182 likes and 11 replies. TOP has not said anything further about ScoutOP or the show.

The reel carries the caption “Some masks don’t fall. They get removed”, with the hashtags #BiggBoss20, #BB20, #ScoutOP and #ScoutArmy. It was posted while ScoutOP remains a contestant in the house. TOP edited the comment after first posting it.

TOP first won the PMGC Grand Finals MVP award in 2022, playing for the Mongolian side GodLike Stalwart. He won it again at PMGC 2025 with Alpha Gaming, becoming the first player to take the award twice. He finished the 2025 Grand Finals with 32 eliminations and an average of 461 damage per match. Krafton also gave him a Porsche Cayenne as part of the MVP prize.

Between those titles he played for Stalwart Esports, which finished second at PMGC 2023, and for Falcons Force. It is not known whether TOP and ScoutOP have a personal connection beyond the game.

The reel follows a difficult stretch for ScoutOP in the house. He reportedly received four punishments after pushing fellow contestant Yung DSA, including the possibility of eviction at any time . The show has not officially confirmed the punishments. Earlier in the season, he faced criticism after an argument with Arishfa Khan during a task.

ScoutOP is one of India’s most-followed gaming creators and a former professional PUBG Mobile player. After an earlier captaincy task, he asked viewers directly for their votes, saying “from now on, I need your support”. Outside the show, Rohit Jagasia said this month that Scout owns 50% of Revenant XSpark .

title: Kaashvi Hits Back at Pages Sending Her Hate: ‘I’ll Have My Say When I’m Ready’
content:
Kaashvi Hiranandani, the gaming creator known online as Kaash Plays, has told the pages criticising her that she will not defend herself until she is ready. “To the pages calling me out and sending me hate, go ahead and villainize me with whatever little context you have,” she wrote on X on 16 November. She added that she was not going to answer “a story you don’t even know in its entirety”, and that some of her critics would later “realise how unfairly you’ve judged me and the situation”. The post had passed 8,500 views and nearly 400 likes within half an hour.

to the pages calling me out and sending me hate, go ahead and villainize me with whatever little context you have. I'm not going to defend myself against a story you don't even know in its entirety. I'll have my say when I'm ready. some of you will realise then how unfairly…

Kaashvi did not name the pages or say which story she meant. Her post came at the end of a weekend that tied her name to ScoutOP’s run on Bigg Boss 20 once again. It happened first on the show itself, and then in a viral clip from her own YouTube channel. She also did not say when she plans to speak, and neither Scout’s team nor Bigg Boss has commented on her post.

Tanmay “Scout” Singh entered the Bigg Boss 20 house in September as the first Indian esports star on the show , and his closeness to fellow contestant Love Gill soon became one of the season’s talking points. On 25 October, Kaashvi entered the house and asked Scout to set boundaries with Love, whom she accused of emotional manipulation. Love denied it, and her team said the next day that she saw Scout as a brother.

Kaashvi apologised on Instagram on 26 October after viewers said she had painted Love unfairly on national television. She said that “some of the words I used were insensitive towards other people involved”, and that she never meant to direct hate at Love. On 6 November, she told viewers on a livestream that she would support Scout “wholeheartedly”, calling it “my last act for him” and “the last dance”. Many fans read that as a break-up, although neither of them has announced one.

Scout’s own time in the house has not been quiet either. He reportedly received four punishments after pushing Yung DSA earlier this month, and after a tough Weekend Ka Vaar on 31 October, his team wrote on Instagram that “storms don’t define legends” but reveal them. The post went up on Scout’s official Instagram account while he was inside the house, and it did not name anyone.

title: LEC : non, Los Ratones ne sera pas de retour en 2027
content:
Les fans de Los Ratones vont devoir patienter avant de revoir leur équipe favorite en LEC. Alors que plusieurs rumeurs évoquaient une possible arrivée de la structure en 2027, Marc « Caedrel » Lamont a tenu à mettre les choses au clair. Selon les informations rapportées par Team aAa , le streamer britannique a confirmé que son organisation ne participerait pas au championnat européen la saison prochaine.

Cette annonce met fin aux spéculations qui entouraient Los Ratones depuis plusieurs semaines. Après avoir découvert le plus haut niveau européen lors du LEC Versus 2026, l’équipe de Caedrel semblait être une candidate potentielle à un retour dans la compétition. Son nom avait notamment été associé à une possible location du slot de Shifters, anciennement Team BDS. Une piste que le principal intéressé a également formellement démentie.

Si Los Ratones est désormais hors course, l’avenir de Shifters reste particulièrement incertain. La structure dispose toujours d’une place en LEC, mais plusieurs rumeurs évoquent depuis quelques semaines une possible cession ou location de son slot. Pour l’heure, aucune opération n’a été officialisée, et l’identité des équipes qui participeront à la saison 2027 n’est pas encore totalement connue.

De son côté, Caedrel ferme donc la porte à un retour immédiat de Los Ratones dans l’élite. Une déception pour les supporters de l’organisation, qui avaient pu suivre ses premiers pas en LEC en début d’année. Reste à savoir quel sera le prochain chapitre du projet et si une nouvelle opportunité se présentera à l’avenir. En attendant, le feuilleton autour de Shifters devrait continuer d’animer l’intersaison européenne.

Après avoir fermement écarté un retour de Los Ratones en #LEC via le spot à louer de Shifters, Caedrel spécule sur l’identité du club qui pourrait récupérer la place : pic.twitter.com/Bc57csALFH

title: LOUD and Vivo Keyd Stars Reach Verbal Agreement Over Xyno Transfer
content:
LOUD and Vivo Keyd Stars have reached a verbal agreement for LOUD to buy top laner Carlos Felipe “Xyno” Ferreira, Sheep Esports reported. The 19 year old has spent the 2026 season at LOUD on loan from Vivo Keyd Stars. He is expected to sign a permanent contract with LOUD in the coming days and stay with the team for 2027. Neither organisation has confirmed the deal.

The two sides had agreed the total fee and the number of instalments when the loan began. Talks stalled over the size of each instalment and the payment dates. The organisations resolved the dispute after further discussions. The fee and the payment schedule have not been disclosed.

Xyno was LOUD’s starting top laner throughout 2026. He played in the CBLOL Cup, both CBLOL splits, First Stand and the Esports World Cup. LOUD lost to LYON in a five-game series at First Stand in March. In August he told Sheep Esports that the rebuilt LOUD side “really want to prove” themselves.

He joined Vivo Keyd Stars Academy in February 2025 after leaving FURIA, where he played for the academy side and made eight appearances for the main roster in CBLOL 2024 Split 1. His Vivo Keyd Stars contract runs until 15 November 2027. He previously competed under the name Fonix.

LOUD’s previous top laner was Leonardo “Robo” Souza, a seven-time CBLOL champion. Robo renewed with LOUD for 2025 after turning down an offer from Vivo Keyd Stars. LOUD has not announced the rest of its 2027 roster, and Vivo Keyd Stars has not commented on the sale.

title: KRAFTON Hires Samsung’s Former Legal Chief and a Top Finance Ministry Official
content:
KRAFTON, the South Korean publisher behind PUBG: Battlegrounds and BGMI, has hired a former senior finance ministry official and a former head of legal at Samsung Electronics. Ahn Sang-yeol, who ran fiscal management at the Ministry of Economy and Finance until 2025, joins as a policy adviser. Kim Jae-hoon, who led Samsung Electronics’ legal team as an executive vice president, becomes KRAFTON’s Head of Legal Affairs and External Relations. The appointments were reported by Korean games outlet Inven on 16 November.

Both men join as unregistered executives, which in Korea means they hold executive titles but do not sit on the company’s board. Ahn’s role is part-time and advisory, while Kim’s is full-time. TalkEsport found no announcement of the hires in KRAFTON’s own newsroom, and neither man has commented publicly. The timing stands out, though, because KRAFTON has spent much of 2026 dealing with legal fights and, more recently, a sharp drop in profit.

Ahn is a career economic official who passed the 39th Higher Civil Service Examination. According to Inven, he worked in the presidential secretariat for science and technology in 2013 and directed the finance ministry’s fiscal management division from 2016 to 2018. He was seconded to the National Assembly’s Strategy and Finance Committee in 2019, and he served as the ministry’s fiscal management officer, a Grade 1 post, in 2024 and 2025. The ministry has since become the Ministry of Finance and Economy .

Kim brings about 14 years of senior legal work inside two Samsung companies. He studied law at Seoul National University, where he earned a bachelor’s and a master’s degree, and later took an LL.M. at Georgetown University. At Samsung Electronics, he rose from vice president of legal and compliance in 2012 to executive vice president of legal affairs by 2021. From 2022 until this year he was executive vice president of legal and contracts at Samsung E&A , the group’s engineering and construction arm.

KRAFTON has already tied part of Kim’s pay to its share price. Inven reported that the company granted him 800 restricted stock units on 28 September. Restricted stock units only turn into shares once set conditions are met, usually after a period of service, so the grant gives Kim a reason to stay.

KRAFTON’s biggest legal problem this year came from Delaware. In March, the Court of Chancery ruled that KRAFTON breached its acquisition agreement with Unknown Worlds by firing the Subnautica 2 studio’s leaders without cause, and it reinstated CEO Ted Gill. The case drew global attention because the ruling described how KRAFTON’s chief executive, Changhan Kim, used ChatGPT while looking for a way out of a $250 million earnout. Our breakdown of the Delaware ruling covers how that plan fell apart.

title: FaZe take a second-half problem to the Singapore Major
content:
Four straight Bo3 defeats, three rounds won in six second halves and a 4-10 map record against the top 20: the numbers FaZe carry into Stage 1.

FaZe Clan will play the PGL Major Singapore on a run of four Bo3 defeats. The last two came on Sunday, when Fnatic and HEROIC put them out of the PGL Cluj-Napoca 2027 Closed Qualifier in 7th-8th place, as we covered in HEROIC’s win over FaZe . Before that they lost 1-2 to FURIA and 1-2 to Falcons at IEM Beijing 2026. How they lost those four series is the bigger worry eight days before their opener against Wildcard .

In six of the eight maps FaZe lost in the streak, they won one round or none after half-time. Three times they were level at 6-6 at the break and finished on six or seven rounds.

The pattern was there before Beijing too. At the RLG Tesla Cup on 29 October, FaZe led GamerLegion 8-4 on Dust2 and lost the map 9-13, before going down 1-2 in the series. The swings do not only go one way: FaZe came back from 2-10 to beat FURIA 13-11 on Ancient, and from 3-9 to force overtime against HEROIC on Mirage. But in the two series that decided their Cluj-Napoca fate, they could not close a map they had drawn level at the half.

Since mid-August, FaZe have played 23 Bo3s and won 11. Their one trophy in that time came at Roman Imperium Cup IX on 10 October, where they beat Sangal, PURE and NAVI Junior twice. Against the bigger names the record is thin. Their Bo3 wins over Legacy at the Esports World Cup and HEROIC at Digital Crusade DraculaN Season 7 are the exceptions in a run that also includes defeats to Vitality, Nemiga, Astralis, BC.Game, magic, Alliance and JiJieHao.

Over the last three months FaZe have played 56 maps and won 27. Against teams in the top 20 of HLTV’s ranking they have won four of 14.

title: nobody and CHICHOO leave EDward Gaming, ending Champions-winning core before Hangzhou
content:
A month after Global Esports handed out a beating to EDward Gaming at VALORANT Champions 2026, captain Wang "nobody" Senxu and controller Wan "CHICHOO" Shunzhi have left the Chinese org. Their exits (which were confirmed on Webo) bring to an end a triumphant five years, during which the group won VALORANT Champions 2024 and cemented their position as the most decorated Chinese org ever.

For a VCT China partner team, losing three starters in a week with the January Kickoff approaching is a heavy rebuild, although rumors suggest Daniel "Rossy" Abedrabbo is set to sign. No official replacements, though, have been named.

🇨🇳 CHICHOO officially concludes his time with 🇨🇳 EDward Gaming He joined EDG way back in 2021 and qualified to 12 international tournaments before his departure. CHICHOO’s tenure with EDG was highlighted by lifting VCT CN’s first ever international trophy at Champions Seoul.

nobody joined EDG on Sept. 7, 2021, beginning as an initiator before taking over in-game leading duties. Eventually, he was trusted with the captaincy. CHICHOO played controller beside him.

Together, they anchored the roster that beat the field on Aug. 25, 2024, making EDG the first organization from China, and from Asia, to lift the Champions trophy. EDG's total winnings sit at $1,592,287.

Both players were still central this year. At Masters London, each played 12 maps, with CHICHOO averaging a 179 average combat score and nobody a 184. However, in a post-match interview after the org’s defeat to Global Esports last month, CHICHOO seemed highly critical, pinpointing the collapse to a lack of communication. Now, just weeks later, he has left the org, though there is no suggestion of a link between the defeat, the reaction and the controller’s exit.

title: LEC in 2027 will have no best-of-ones, only Bo3s and Bo5s
content:
The League of Legends EMEA Championship (LEC) is making some changes in 2027, including complete abolition of best-of-ones from the domestic league. All three LEC 2027 splits will only be comprised of best-of-threes and best-of-fives, while familiar mechanics like Fearless Draft and First Selection will return.

LEC 2027 will once again have three splits: Winter, Spring , and Summer .

LEC Winter 2027 begins Jan. 15 . The top teams from this split will compete in First Stand: All In , although the exact number of teams to qualify are still currently unconfirmed.

Unlike in 2026 where the Winter split had a different format than the rest of the year, all three LEC 2027 splits will have the same format:

All matches will feature Fearless Draft and First Selection mechanics, as is the current standard for professional League of Legends play.

“By keeping the focus on longer series, we’re giving teams more opportunities to adapt, develop strategies, and demonstrate their strengths over the course of a match,” outlined the LEC in a press release sent to esports.gg. “The format also provides a competitive environment that more closely mirrors international play, helping teams prepare for the challenges ahead.”

title: Esports World Cup : League of Legends encore au rendez-vous en 2027
content:
L’Esports World Cup continue de dévoiler les jeux qui composeront son édition 2027. Sans grande surprise, League of Legends sera une nouvelle fois de la partie, confirmant sa présence pour la quatrième année consécutive depuis le lancement de l’événement en 2024. Jusqu’ici, les équipes sud-coréennes ont fait main basse sur le trophée, avec trois champions différents : T1 en 2024, Gen.G en 2025 et Dplus KIA en 2026.

La dernière édition, organisée à Paris, avait notamment été marquée par le parcours exceptionnel de Dplus KIA. Battus d’entrée par AG.AL, les Coréens avaient renversé la situation en éliminant successivement FURIA, G2, Bilibili Gaming et Gen.G. En finale, ils avaient surclassé la Karmine Corp (3-0), pourtant portée par son public français. Une victoire qui leur avait offert leur premier titre international depuis cinq ans, avec Smash élu MVP de la compétition.

Pour 2027, plusieurs formations auront à cœur de détrôner les représentants de la LCK. C’est notamment le cas de Bilibili Gaming, tout juste sacré champion du monde après sa victoire face à Gen.G (3-1) en finale des Worlds 2026. Après plusieurs finales internationales perdues, les Chinois ont enfin retrouvé les sommets et pourraient désormais viser un premier sacre à l’Esports World Cup.

Hanwha Life Esports sera également une équipe à surveiller, après son titre au MSI 2026 et son élimination prématurée en quarts de finale de l’EWC face à T1. Du côté de la LPL, AG.AL espère aussi prendre sa revanche après sa défaite contre la Karmine Corp à Paris. Déjà vainqueur du classement général des clubs en 2026, la structure chinoise pourrait chercher à enrichir son palmarès sur League of Legends. Reste désormais à connaître le format, les dates et les équipes qualifiées pour cette quatrième édition.

The Rift is calling again. League of Legends is back for EWC27. pic.twitter.com/2Ol4TlqHc7

title: Madrid and Bucharest bring FACEIT’s new European servers to four
content:
Spain and Romania join Türkiye and Poland, and all four locations go live with Season 10 on 9 December.

FACEIT will open four new server locations in Europe on 9 December, the day Season 10 starts. Bucharest and Madrid are the latest additions on the platform’s Season 10 page , after Istanbul was announced on Friday at 18:00 CET and Warsaw on Saturday at 18:00 .

FACEIT says the Romanian and Spanish servers are there “to improve connectivity across Europe”. Istanbul means players in Türkiye “can play closer to home”, and Warsaw is meant to help players in Eastern Europe get a better connection.

Announcing the second new FACEIT server location coming to Europe. Live December 09 with Season 10. Follow each update as it is announced at https://t.co/qfvOsqDKau pic.twitter.com/yeQnIimm2x

The four cities follow the four North American locations announced on Thursday: Atlanta, Los Angeles, New York and Seattle. That makes eight new locations for Season 10.

The Warsaw announcement came in a Polish video presented by Kamil “Rocky”, who has worked with leagues for eight years. He called Poland one of the most active communities on the platform, and set out two rules for when players will actually get the new server.
