title: Cryogen Staying at FlyQuest Is Only Half the Story
content:
A year ago most fans had never heard of him. Now FlyQuest are reportedly building around him. Sheep Esports sources say Rookie of the Year Cryogen is staying for LCS 2027, but the rest of the roster is still a mystery.

Sheep Esports reports, citing sources, that support Michael "Cryogen" Luu will stay with FlyQuest for the 2027 LCS season. He is coming off a debut year that earned him Rookie of the Year. Sheep Esports lists him at 19 years old, with a contract that runs until November 2028.

A year ago, most fans had never heard his name. Now he is one of the few players FlyQuest have chosen to build around, after a season that ended without a trip to Worlds.

This was not FlyQuest's first choice. They wanted to keep Alan "Busio" Cwalina, but he turned down an extension and signed with Karmine Corp, as Sheep Esports reported at the time. FlyQuest then looked at several options, and Cryogen was their main target.

They already knew him. The organization had followed him through combines and scouting, and he had impressed in tryouts. That led to a spot as a substitute for FlyQuest NZXT in North America Challengers, and Sheep Esports reported he joined the main roster's preparation before the LTA North Split 2 Finals, which FlyQuest went on to win.

When the LCS chance came, the former DarkZero Dragonsteel support also had an offer to play in the ERLs for G2 NORD, G2 Esports' academy team. He decided to stay in North America.

title: Zeus set to replace xavi8k as XLG back out of verbal deal
content:
Xi Lai Gaming are going for the Team Secret duelist they first passed over, and the Pacific Stage 2 champion is a free agent again.

Neither XLG, xavi8k nor Zeus has confirmed anything. Sheep gives no reason for the U-turn, but Zeus is not a new name. In its first report on the deal, Sheep had already said Zeus was considered for the same import slot. XLG first picked the caller, then changed their minds.

title: karrigan: “People have written us off for the major”
content:
Falcons’ captain called the season “incredibly disappointing” after two Asian events without a final, but says he still trusts the team.

Finn “ karrigan ” Andersen wrote on X on Sunday at 13:06 CET that he is “incredibly disappointed” in Team Falcons’ season, a day after FURIA knocked them out of the BLAST Rivals semi-finals in Hong Kong.

Incredibly disappointed in our performance this season, our Asia trip back to back has been far from what we wanted to achieve. One tournament left this season to show that besides all the defeats, we can still show up and play great CS. People have written us off for the…

The “Asia trip back to back” he refers to is IEM Beijing, where Falcons finished 7th-8th, and Hong Kong, where they went out in 3rd-4th. The 36-year-old had a hard event himself: he went 19-36 in the 2-0 semi-final loss and finished with an HLTV rating of 0.84, as we wrote when he answered BLAST’s retirement post with a single “Ok”.

Falcons have not reached a final since they beat FURIA 3-0 to win the IEM Cologne Major in June, and coach Danny “zonic” Sørensen called the season “not good enough” after the exit. Ilya “m0NESY” Osipov had already told BLAST’s broadcast that the months since Cologne had been “very frustrating” .

The PGL Major Singapore is the last event of Falcons’ season, and they arrive as defending champions.

title: LEC : on connaît le prix du transfert de SkewMond à la Karmine Corp
content:
Annoncé depuis plusieurs jours dans le viseur de la Karmine Corp, Rudy « SkewMond » Semaan aurait finalement obtenu gain de cause. Selon les dernières informations du leaker Aron , G2 Esports et la structure française seraient parvenus à un accord définitif pour le transfert du jungler de 21 ans. Le montant de l’opération avoisinerait les 300 000 euros, une somme conséquente pour permettre au Blue Wall de récupérer l’un des talents français les plus prometteurs du LEC.

Pourtant, l’opération était encore loin d’être acquise il y a quelques jours. Team Vitality aurait tenté de s’immiscer dans les négociations en proposant à G2 un échange impliquant son toplaner Naak Nako. Une possibilité qui aurait particulièrement intéressé les Samouraïs, désireux de renforcer leur toplane. Mais SkewMond aurait refusé de rejoindre la Ruche, affichant clairement sa préférence pour le projet de la Karmine Corp. Les discussions se seraient ensuite compliquées après certaines déclarations de Kameto en stream, qui auraient poussé G2 à revoir temporairement ses exigences financières à la hausse.

Malgré ces tensions, les différentes parties auraient finalement réussi à trouver un terrain d’entente durant le week-end. Selon nos informations, SkewMond se serait également accordé avec la Karmine Corp sur les conditions de son futur contrat. Le Français devrait s’engager pour au moins deux saisons, avec de possibles clauses de prolongation. Un investissement important qui témoignerait de la volonté du club de construire son projet autour du jeune jungler.

Son arrivée entraînerait logiquement le départ de Yike, titulaire dans la jungle de la Karmine Corp en 2026. Le Suédois serait désormais tout proche de rejoindre Fnatic, dans le cadre d’un mercato particulièrement animé sur la scène européenne. Après avoir conservé son midlaner kyeahoo, le Blue Wall s’apprêterait donc à réaliser un nouveau mouvement majeur pour préparer la saison 2027. Reste désormais à attendre les annonces officielles des différentes organisations pour confirmer la conclusion de ce long feuilleton.

Sources: Skewmond has come to an agreement with Karmine Corp ahead of 2027 Both organizations involved in this deal have also came to an agreement on the buyout which is around 300 000 € #MilanoFirst pic.twitter.com/4OpHmdOMEZ

title: BLAST return to Hong Kong for a third straight year in 2027
content:
BLAST Rivals goes back to AsiaWorld-Arena from 8 to 14 November 2027, after two sold-out editions in the city.

Seven days in November 2027 are now booked. BLAST will take BLAST Rivals back to AsiaWorld-Arena in Hong Kong from 8 to 14 November, the third year in a row the city hosts the event. The organiser announced it on Sunday, the last day of this year’s edition.

All good things come in threes, and we're coming back for a third year, Hong Kong! 🙌 🇭🇰 Hong Kong 🏟️ AsiaWorld-Arena 📅 8th-14th November 2027 #BLASTPremier pic.twitter.com/E3fZ63tPiF

BLAST say both Hong Kong editions sold out. The 2025 debut drew more than 30,000 fans across three live audience days and, according to an independent report by the Education University of Hong Kong, over HK$600 million in economic impact. Ticketing for 2027 will be announced in the coming months.

FURIA have won both so far. On Sunday they swept Team Spirit to become the first team to defend a Rivals title, and the Grand Final peaked at 845K viewers, according to Esports Charts .

“We can’t wait to return for the third edition in 2027 and make the event even bigger and better,” said James Woollard, BLAST’s VP of Destinations and Market Development.

title: Demon1: “No trials, no team, no one wants me”
content:
The 2023 world champion says he has had no trials for the 2027 VCT season, four days before North America’s Kickoff qualifier reaches its Swiss stage.

Zero trials. That is how many Max “Demon1” Mazanov says he has had ahead of the 2027 VCT season, three years after he was named MVP of Valorant Champions 2023 with Evil Geniuses. A clip of the American saying so on his stream was posted to r/ValorantCompetitive on Monday 00:51 CET and passed 570 upvotes within hours.

title: Worlds 2026 : une chute d’audience de 42 % pour la finale
content:
Le spectacle était au rendez-vous à Brooklyn, mais les audiences n’ont pas suivi. Samedi soir, Bilibili Gaming a remporté le premier titre mondial de son histoire en dominant Gen.G (3-1), mettant fin à cinq années de disette pour la Chine. Pourtant, cette finale des Worlds 2026 n’a attiré que 3 943 920 spectateurs simultanés à son pic, selon les données d’ Esports Charts . Un chiffre qui exclut les plateformes chinoises et qui tranche avec les records établis ces dernières années.

La comparaison avec l’édition précédente est particulièrement frappante. En 2025, la finale entre T1 et KT Rolster avait rassemblé près de 6,75 millions de spectateurs simultanés, soit une baisse de 42 % en un an. L’audience moyenne du tournoi recule également de 19 %, à 1,22 million de spectateurs. En revanche, le nombre total d’heures visionnées résiste davantage, avec 129,7 millions d’heures cumulées (-3 %). Une relative stabilité qui s’explique notamment par une durée de diffusion plus importante : près de 107 heures cette année, contre moins de 89 heures en 2025.

3.9M Peak Viewers on #Worlds2026 Grand Finals @BilibiliGaming vs @GenG_KR Stats excl. Chinese streaming platforms pic.twitter.com/egksmSZM5f

Plusieurs facteurs peuvent expliquer cette baisse spectaculaire. D’abord, l’organisation de la compétition en Amérique du Nord, avec des horaires moins favorables au public asiatique, historiquement très important sur League of Legends. Mais surtout, l’absence de T1 en finale semble avoir privé Riot Games de son principal moteur d’audience. Après trois sacres mondiaux consécutifs, Faker et ses coéquipiers ont été éliminés par Bilibili Gaming en demi-finale, au terme d’une rencontre qui avait tout de même attiré 3,61 millions de spectateurs simultanés.

Le quart de finale entre T1 et la Karmine Corp complète d’ailleurs le podium des rencontres les plus suivies du tournoi, avec 2,8 millions de spectateurs au maximum. Des chiffres qui témoignent de l’attractivité exceptionnelle de la formation sud-coréenne, même lorsque celle-ci ne va pas au bout de la compétition. Conséquence de cette baisse d’audience, les Worlds perdent également leur place de tournoi esport le plus regardé de l’année. Un titre désormais détenu par le M7 World Championship de Mobile Legends: Bang Bang, qui avait culminé à 5,68 millions de spectateurs en janvier 2026.

Ce recul intervient alors que Riot Games vient justement de dévoiler plusieurs changements importants pour son circuit international. En 2027, la saison débutera en Chine avec une édition exceptionnelle de First Stand, baptisée « All In », qui réunira davantage d’équipes. Le Mid-Season Invitational fera ensuite son retour en Europe, à Valence, avant des Worlds organisés conjointement au Japon et en Corée du Sud. Nagoya accueillera la phase suisse, tandis que les playoffs se dérouleront sur le sol coréen, avec une finale attendue à Séoul.

title: FFWS 2026 Global Finals Knockout Phase 2: Date, Teams, Format, and More
content:
Knockout Stage Phase 2 of the Free Fire World Series (FFWS) 2026 Global Finals runs in Bangkok from 19 to 22 November. Eighteen teams take part, and eight of them will reach the Grand Finals at BITEC LIVE on 28 November. Buriram United Esports enter Phase 2 top of the table after finishing Phase 1 with 647 points. The other 10 teams drop into the Last Chance stage on 27 November.

Phase 2 splits the 18 survivors into four pools based on their Phase 1 rankings. The top 12 teams start on the first day, and the six teams placed 13th to 18th join two at a time over the next three days. Two teams qualify for the Grand Finals each day. The event carries a $1,200,000 prize pool.

Each Phase 2 matchday has six matches. The top two teams on each day move to the Grand Finals, and the remaining 10 carry on to the next day. Two new teams from the lower pools enter each day, so every matchday has 12 teams in the lobby.

Matches use the standard FFWS scoring. A win is worth 12 placement points, second place nine and third place eight, with one point for every elimination. The scale drops to one point for 10th place and nothing for 11th and 12th.

Buriram United Esports, the defending champions, finished Phase 1 with 647 points, 11 more than LOS in second. Fluxo W7M were third with 633 points, and P Esports fourth with 599. The 12 teams in Pool 1 all play on the opening day, which gives them the most chances to qualify before the Last Chance stage.

Resurrection Esports and GunDynasty both finished on 411 points, and Resurrection took 13th place. GunDynasty reached that total despite a 15-point penalty after the opening day of Phase 1. Garena docked them for deliberately dying in the zone in the sixth match.

title: Vanshaj Sharma Interview: “I Was Here for Revenge,” Red Bull Wings Cup India Champion on Miami
content:
Vanshaj Sharma will represent India at the Red Bull Wings Cup World Final in Miami after winning the EA Sports FC 27 India National Final at Kettle Studio in Bengaluru on 15 November. The RNTX player beat Saransh Jain 2–0 in the best-of-three final, winning the games 5–1 and 4–1. The title came two days after he returned from the FC Pro Open Global Qualifier in London, and less than two weeks after RNTX signed him for that event.

Minutes after lifting the trophy, Vanshaj spoke to TalkEsport’s Pranav Nalawade in Bengaluru. He talked about beating a close friend in the final, the practice he brought back from London, the Esports Nations Cup qualifier he missed by one game in August, and the part of his game he wants to fix before Miami. The interview was conducted in Hindi and English and has been translated and lightly edited for clarity.

TalkEsport: Congratulations. You have your ticket to Miami and the responsibility of representing India. How do you see an opportunity this big?

Vanshaj Sharma: Like I said, I am very overwhelmed with emotions. This is a very big thing for me, and my emotions are overflowing right now. But I am very proud of myself, and as I said, I will make my country very proud when I go there. So yeah, I am really excited.

TalkEsport: Saransh is one of India’s most experienced FC players. What does beating him in the final mean to you?

Vanshaj Sharma: He is a very good friend of mine. We have been competing against each other back to back for many years, so it feels bad to beat him too. But in the end we are opponents. Playing with him is always a good experience. GGs to him.

title: HEROIC knock FaZe out of Cluj-Napoca qualifier nine days before the Major
content:
Brollan led a 2-0 win in the lower bracket, and FaZe go to Singapore on four straight series defeats.

Two series in one day were all FaZe Clan got at the PGL Cluj-Napoca 2027 Closed Qualifier. HEROIC beat them 16-13 on Mirage and 13-8 on Ancient in the first round of the lower bracket on Sunday 15 November, their second defeat in the double-elimination bracket. FaZe finish 7th-8th and will not be in Romania.

FaZe were one of the six teams PGL invited to the closed qualifier from Valve’s European standings, as we covered when PGL confirmed the Cluj-Napoca teams . Mirage was their own pick, and they trailed 3-9 at the half. They won nine of the 12 rounds after the switch to force overtime at 12-12, but HEROIC took the extra period 4-1. Antonio “MartinezSa” Martínez went 26-16 with 84.2 ADR on the map.

On HEROIC’s Ancient pick it was 6-6 at the break before HEROIC won seven of the last nine rounds. Ludvig “ Brollan ” Brolin went 22-12 with 101.4 ADR on the map and finished the series 45-32 with 94.4 ADR and 88.0% KAST. No FaZe player ended the series with more kills than deaths. JBOEN came closest at 31-32, but with 54.2 ADR, the lowest on the server.

FaZe had dropped into the lower bracket earlier the same day. Fnatic beat them 2-1 in the upper bracket quarter-final, and both lost maps went the same way: 6-6 at the half on Fnatic’s Anubis pick, then 1-7 after the switch, and 6-6 on the Ancient decider before a 0-7 second half. Coach Niclas “enkay J” Krumhorn played Anubis in place of jcobbb.

Volodymyr “mazay” Iorhachov led Fnatic with 52-35 and 96.9 ADR. On FaZe’s side, JBOEN went 46-34, while Russel “ Twistzz ” Van Dulken finished level at 37-37.

title: TFT Set 19 Prismatic Tour hits high note with musical traits and champions
content:

TFT Set 19, also known as Prismatic Tour, releases on Dec. 2 on PC and mobile. This launch features 94 champions and more than 20 music genres.

Prismatic Tour features the unlock mechanic from Lore & Legends, allowing you to add unlockable units to your champion pool. For example, you can field three Heartsteel champions to unlock Alune. Those who love Smeech and wish to experience the Jazz trait, meanwhile, can unlock him by having eight active traits.

“Take Smeech, for example, our legendary Jazz Renegade, swinging all the way over from our Arcane set in fedora-clad style. To unlock this smeechy smeecher, you’ll need to have eight or more traits active,” head of gameplay Alex “Riot Bluevelvet” Cole explained. “While difficult, it’s something you’ll want to do to maximize the Jazz trait, which is back from Set 10 to give stats based on your total active traits.”

Players who wish to experience the unlock mechanic at its fullest can try for an all-Yordle Hyperpop roster as well. While most TFT Set 19 traits have about two unlockable units, Hyperpop has all unlockables save for the 1-cost Ziggs.

Each member of the Hyperpop lineup helps unlock the next one until acquiring Ziggs, Kobuko, Tristana, and Lulu. Then, you can 3-star all these Yordles to unlock Teemo. Rerolling and increasing the star level of these Hyperpop champions also contributes to the Hype Meter for loot.

title: Zombies Aren’t Real Lets You Stop an Outbreak in Real Cities, and Steam Players Love It
content:
Zombies Aren’t Real, a top-down strategy game about stopping a zombie outbreak in real cities, has made a strong start on Steam since its release at the end of last week. The Early Access game from Jogamedev, the studio behind Spellmasons, launched on 13 November and holds an Overwhelmingly Positive rating, with 96% of 611 user reviews recommending it on its Steam page . It reached an all-time peak of 5,782 concurrent players on 14 November, according to SteamDB , and was still above 5,300 players when TalkEsport checked. It costs $9.99, with a 10% launch discount until 20 November.

The idea is simple to explain and hard to master. You look down on a real city from above before an infection breaks out, spend limited resources on defences, and then try to contain the horde while saving as many civilians as you can. Every mission is scored on lives saved, which turns each decision about where to place troops into a question of who you can afford to leave outside the line.

The most distinctive feature is where the outbreaks happen. Missions take place in large real-world cities built by the developer, and the game already supports custom maps through Steam Workshop. Jogamedev says custom maps can pull in public geographic data for zip codes worldwide, so players are not limited to the cities that ship with the game.

The first Workshop campaigns show where the developer’s head is. The four maps listed so far, all made by the developer, are Sighișoara in Romania, Auckland in New Zealand, and Nördlingen and Wemding in Bavaria. Sighișoara and Nördlingen are both famous for their surviving medieval town walls, which makes them obvious places to hold back a horde. Workshop pages for the game are available on its Steam Workshop hub .

For players in India, the zip code support is the most interesting part. If postal codes outside the US and Europe work as the store page suggests, Indian players could build and defend maps of their own neighbourhoods. The developer has not shown an Indian city yet, and TalkEsport has not tested how well the map data works for Indian postal codes.

Your tools are a mix of ground forces and air support. The Steam page lists snipers, turrets, mortar squads and garrisons on the ground, with bombers and gatling gun helicopters available as air strikes. Those strikes have to be aimed carefully, because the game counts civilian casualties as well as zombie kills, and players can also place safe zones and gates to protect people from the spread.

title: Is Minecraft 2 Real? Mojang Just Laid Out Very Different Plans
content:
Early today several reports emerged of Mojang, building a full-scale “Minecraft 2”, the studio’s own plans, which was published the same day, point somewhere else entirely. The post from Chaos Crave on Sunday said the sequel is being built “from the ground up on a brand-new engine” for PC, PlayStation 6 and the next Xbox. It credited unnamed “insiders” with details such as realistic water physics, dynamic weather disasters and travel between dimensions without loading screens.

The rumour spread quickly because it promises something many players have wanted for years. Minecraft has sold more than 425 million copies, according to Xbox, and Xbox chief executive Asha Sharma said in September that over 300,000 people play it for the first time every day . A clean-slate sequel would be one of the biggest announcements in gaming, which is exactly why the lack of a named source matters.

The platforms named in the post raise questions of their own. Sony has not announced the PlayStation 6, and its chief executive said in May that the console’s release date and price had not been decided . Microsoft’s next console, Project Helix, will only reach developers as alpha hardware from 2027 , and Xbox described it this weekend as a console that can also play PC games .

Xbox’s 25th anniversary magazine, released on 15 November and free to read on Xbox Wire , includes a long feature on what comes next for Minecraft. It quotes Kayleen Walters, president of Xbox’s XP division and former president of Mojang, at length. Her account centres on extending the current game rather than replacing it.

The biggest piece of that plan is the Sift, a new dimension that Mojang announced at Minecraft Live on 26 September. It debuted in Minecraft Dungeons II, which launched in September, and arrives in the main game on Minecraft Java and Bedrock next year. The first Dungeons found around 30 million players, Walters said, which showed Mojang there was appetite for Minecraft in other genres. Walters said Mojang wanted “the most significant addition to the Minecraft universe in 15 years” to debut somewhere players had to go and experience for themselves.

Walters also stressed continuity with what players already have. Minecraft runs on roughly 20 platforms, and she said Mojang treats every player “as equally important, whatever platform they play on”. She described long-running save files as “digital heirlooms”, adding that everything Mojang ships “has to be safe for a world someone has been building since yesterday or for decades”.

title: Jensen Huang Is Weighing a Return as Nvidia CEO
content:
Jensen Huang is considering a return as Nvidia’s chief executive, only days after he resigned, the Financial Times reported on Sunday. Citing people familiar with the matter, the newspaper said Huang has discussed the possibility of coming back with confidants. One of his allies is reportedly assembling a group of Silicon Valley executives, described as a “war room”, to lobby Nvidia’s board for his reinstatement and to seek support from the White House. TalkEsport has not seen a public response to the report from Huang or Nvidia, and the FT’s sources were not named.

The FT report lands at an awkward moment for the company. Huang stepped down on 12 November after reports about his relationship with Alice Huang, the former Megaspeed executive at the centre of a chip export scandal. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been running Nvidia on an interim basis since then, according to the company’s announcement . The board has said it is choosing a search firm and has not formally approached any candidates for the permanent job. The FT’s own summary says tech supporters are now lobbying the chipmaker’s board to reinstate its former chief executive.

The campaign for Huang’s return was already loud before Sunday’s report. Elon Musk said last week that he was signing a petition to reinstate him, and the Stand with Jensen petition has circulated widely since. Musk has also said that hiring Huang himself “would be an honour” , a sign of how much of his standing in the industry has survived the scandal. Ruby on Rails creator David Heinemeier Hansson added his voice on Sunday, writing that “we need @JensenHuang back at NVIDIA” because “the free world depends on it”.

Some of Nvidia’s investors have been pushing in the same direction. Altimeter Capital’s Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management’s Gavin Baker wrote to the board asking it to keep Huang’s return on the table and avoid a rushed replacement. Inside the company, 88% of Nvidia staff who answered a Blind survey before his resignation said he should stay.

What the FT describes goes further than public support. An organised group of executives lobbying the board, and asking the White House to back them, would turn a petition into a direct pressure campaign. Accounts of the FT story published so far do not name the ally behind the “war room” or the executives involved, or say whether the White House has responded.

The biggest obstacle to a comeback is already out in the open. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Sunday that Nvidia needs “a dramatic shakeup” and should hire an outside chief executive. He also wants answers from the board within 10 days on whether the company pushed “seemingly illicit” chip sales to China, a window that runs to around 25 November.

Worlds 2026 Final just recorded its lowest peak in 6 years at 3.98 million
content:
The Worlds 2026 final drew the smallest peak audience for a League of Legends World Championship since 2020. Bilibili Gaming’s 3-1 win over Gen.G at the Barclays Center in New York peaked at 3.98 million viewers, according to Esports Charts, whose figures leave out Chinese streaming platforms. That is roughly 2.8 million fewer than last year’s final and about 3 million below the record of 6.94 million set in 2024. The drop came on the night BLG won their first world title , and it has a few clear explanations.

Esports Charts counts official broadcasts and co-streams together, which is why individual streamers matter so much to these totals. It first reported a 3.9 million peak for the final on Saturday night, then put the figure at 3.98 million the next day. Its numbers show the audience building through the series, from 3.1 million during game one to 3.49 million in game three, before the peak in the deciding fourth game. The figure ties 2019’s final between FunPlus Phoenix and G2 Esports, which also peaked at 3.98 million.

The clearest pattern in the data is T1. Faker’s team played in every Worlds final from 2022 to 2025, and those four finals are the only ones to have passed 5 million peak viewers. The team also reached the 2016 and 2017 finals as SK Telecom T1, when Worlds audiences were far smaller across the board. This year, BLG knocked T1 out 3-1 in the semi-finals , ending their hopes of a fourth straight title before the final in Brooklyn.

The weaker numbers were already visible before the final began. Esports Charts compared peaks before each grand final , and 2026 stood at 3.6 million, against 3.9 million in 2025, 4.9 million in 2024 and 4.3 million in 2023. That 3.6 million peak came from T1’s semi-final against BLG, so the biggest audience of the tournament still belonged to a T1 series even after they were gone.

Gen.G bring a loyal Korean following, and BLG won First Stand earlier this year, but neither has T1’s global pull. TalkEsport’s Worlds 2026 hub shows how open the bracket was, with LYON and Karmine Corp also reaching the knockouts. A final between two strong teams without the sport’s biggest star was unlikely to match the T1 years, however good the series turned out to be.

The start time made the problem worse for Asian fans in particular. The final began at 2 PM Eastern time on Saturday, which was 3 AM in China, as BLG’s own match post confirmed, and 4 AM in South Korea. In Vietnam, home of the night’s second-biggest co-stream, it started at 2 AM, while fans in India had to stay up until 12:30 AM, as TalkEsport’s grand final guide set out.

title: TenZ Wants VALORANT to Copy League’s Pro View After Knight’s Worlds-Winning POV: ‘Can Learn a Lot’
content:
TenZ wants VALORANT esports to copy one of League of Legends’ simplest ideas. On Sunday, the T1 star quoted a LoL Esports post that shared the full pro view of Knight’s game from Bilibili Gaming’s title-winning Worlds 2026 final. “It would be so cool seeing something like this in VALORANT, can learn a lot from watching someone’s POV,” TenZ wrote . His post came only days after T1 signed him to return to professional play in VCT Pacific for the 2027 season.

It would be so cool seeing something like this in VALORANT, can learn a lot from watching someone’s POV https://t.co/WkG03IjJdK

The LoL Esports post invited fans to “check out the FULL PRO VIEW of Knight’s Worlds-winning game 4 against GEN”. The video runs for almost 43 minutes and shows only what BLG’s mid laner saw on his own screen, from his camera movement to his ability usage and minimap checks. BLG beat Gen.G 3-1 at the Barclays Center in New York on Saturday to win the title, and game four was the one that sealed the organisation’s first world title.

LoL Esports shares pro view footage like this so fans can follow a single player instead of the main broadcast. The value is in the details that a broadcast misses, because an observer has to switch between ten players and cannot stay with one for long. A full game from one player’s screen shows every decision that player makes, including the quiet ones between fights.

VALORANT’s official broadcasts are built around a different approach. VCT coverage on VALORANT Esports follows an observer feed that cuts between players as rounds develop, and most player perspective content comes from clips or from players’ own streams. Riot has not announced a pro view series for VCT, and TenZ framed the idea as something he would like to see rather than something that already exists.

His point is easy to understand for anyone who has tried to learn the game from a broadcast. In a tactical shooter, the most useful lessons often happen before a fight starts, in where a player holds their crosshair, when they check a corner and how they time their utility. An observer usually cuts away from those moments to follow the action elsewhere, which is exactly the detail a full POV would keep.

title: Punch The Walls Lets You Fist-Fight Your Way Out of Prison for $2.99, and Steam Look-Alikes Are Already Queuing Up
content:
Punch The Walls is a $2.99 Steam game in which you escape a concrete prison cell by punching through the walls with your bare hands. Developer BoomGames released it on 6 November, and its Steam page shows a Very Positive rating, with 80% of 324 user reviews recommending it at the time of writing. Its loop fits in one line: punch, collect the rubble, sell it, upgrade, and punch harder. At least three similar wall-breaking games are now listed on Steam as upcoming releases, and one of them may even have come first.

You wake up locked in a concrete cell with no visible way out, and your fists are the only tool you have. Every punch breaks part of a voxel wall into cubes, which you vacuum up and feed into a shredder that turns them into cash. That money buys stronger, faster punches with more reach, as well as a better vacuum and an upgraded shredder, so each wall you break pays for the next one. The rubble is physics-based too, so broken cubes tumble and pile up on the floor until you clear them.

The tools grow more destructive as you dig. Steam’s feature list includes charged punches, dynamite and C4 for harder rock, and the punches and vacuum both have their own upgrade paths. There are eight rock types to break, and buried gold, watches and crowns add a reason to tunnel in every direction rather than straight for an exit.

There is a light mystery on top of the mining. Each prison is procedurally generated, and notes left behind by earlier prisoners hold the code to the door. That gives each run a reason to explore rather than simply dig, because the way out is written down somewhere inside the walls.

The low price is only part of its appeal. The minimum Windows specification asks for an Intel Core i5-4590 or AMD Ryzen 3 1200, 4GB of RAM and a GeForce GTX 750 Ti or Radeon R7 260X. That puts it within reach of PCs that are more than a decade old. It needs just 1GB of storage, and BoomGames also lists a macOS version for Apple M1 or quad-core Intel Macs with 8GB of RAM.

Interface text is available in English and 11 other languages, although there is no full voice audio to localise. Steam tags place it among incremental, destruction and physics games, with mining, voxel and escape room labels alongside them. The game is single-player only, and its tags lean towards relaxed, casual play rather than a stiff challenge.

title: TSG Pros Eliminated From FFWS 2026 Global Finals, Two Points Short of Last Chance
content:
TSG Pros have been eliminated from the Free Fire World Series (FFWS) 2026 Global Finals in Bangkok. The Indian side finished 21st of 24 teams in Knockout Stage Phase 1 with 315 points when the stage ended on 15 November. Stellar Esport took 20th place, the last spot in the Last Chance stage, with 317 points. TSG Pros missed that place by two points.

TSG Pros scored 71 points in their final session, their best return of the stage. It was not enough to close the gap left by a slow first week. Garena’s format sends the bottom four teams home after Phase 1, so TSG Pros leave with ParadoX Gaming, Total Winner Esports and Pirate Esports. The organisation has not commented on the result.

TSG Pros played six sessions across two weeks in Group A, alongside Stellar Esport, Total Winner Esports, Buriram United Esports, ONIC Olympus and GunDynasty. They opened with 34 points on 6 November and finished the first day bottom of the overall table. They had 122 points and sat 21st at the end of Week 1 of the knockout stage , 30 points behind GunDynasty in 20th.

Week 2 brought 193 points from three sessions, against 122 in the first week. GunDynasty, who were docked 15 points after the opening day for deliberately dying to the zone, climbed to 14th with 411 points. Horaa Esports finished 19th on 334, taking the other Last Chance place.

TSG Pros qualified as India’s third seed after finishing third at the TEZ FFMIC 2026 Fall in Noida in September. They topped out on 146 points in the regular FFMIC table, five behind Resurrection on 151. Team Apex Gaming won the FFMIC 2026 Fall title with a final-match Booyah in Champion Rush.

Team Apex Gaming finished 18th with 360 points and stayed in the main draw. Defending champions Buriram United Esports topped the overall FFWS 2026 Global Finals standings with 546 points and 10 Booyahs. Knockout Stage Phase 2 runs from 19 to 22 November, and the Last Chance stage is on 27 November. The Global Finals carry a $1,200,000 prize pool, and Garena has not yet published the payout for teams eliminated in Phase 1.

title: Xbox at 25 in Charts: Every Console Launched in November, and Series X|S Needs Until 2028 to Beat the 360
content:
Xbox turned 25 on 15 November, a quarter of a century after the original console went on sale in North America alongside Halo: Combat Evolved. Microsoft marked the date with a 116-page anniversary magazine and a numbered limited-edition console, while Geoff Keighley congratulated “everyone who helped build Xbox over the past quarter century”. TalkEsport went through that magazine page by page and checked Microsoft’s own launch records to build the charts and timeline below. Several of the details, from a staff-only launch console to the original plan for a 20-year lifespan, come straight from Xbox’s own pages rather than from older histories.

The numbers also show a pattern that is easy to miss. All four of its home consoles launched in North America in November, within 12 days of each other on the calendar, and Xbox Live arrived exactly one year after the first console. The record for the longest-serving Xbox generation still belongs to the Xbox 360, and the current Series X|S needs two more years to take it.

Microsoft’s launch announcements put the Xbox 360’s North American release at 22 November 2005 and Xbox One’s at 22 November 2013 . Series X|S followed on 10 November 2020 , while the original Xbox had gone on sale on 15 November 2001. Xbox Live arrived in stores on 15 November 2002 , one year to the day after the console it ran on. No other month appears anywhere in that list, so every Xbox has launched in the run-up to the holiday shopping season.

TalkEsport then measured how long each console stayed the newest Xbox, counting from its North American launch to its successor’s. The original Xbox lasted 1,468 days, just over four years, before the Xbox 360 replaced it. The 360 then held the top spot for exactly eight years, or 2,922 days, while Xbox One managed 2,545 days, almost seven years.

Series X|S turned six on 10 November, and by Xbox’s 25th birthday it had been the newest Xbox for 2,196 days, still 726 days short of the 360. If Microsoft’s next console does not reach shops before 11 November 2028, Series X|S will become the longest-serving Xbox generation. Xbox has said alpha hardware for Project Helix will reach developers from 2027, but it has not given the console a release date.

The table lists 25 milestones in order, with the source for each one. Most come from Microsoft’s own announcements or from the anniversary magazine, which was written by the Xbox Wire team with editors from across Xbox and is free to read on Xbox Wire . Where the magazine gives a year but no exact date, the table uses the year.

title: dupreeh and NEO head HLTV’s Hall of Fame class as kennyS misses out
content:
Ksharp becomes the first North American inductee, while kennyS is passed over for the third year running.

Four names out of 10. HLTV has announced that Kyle “Ksharp” Miller, Keun-Chul “solo” Kang, Filip “NEO” Kubski and Peter “dupreeh” Rasmussen make up the Counter-Strike Hall of Fame’s Class of 2026, picked from the ballot we covered when the nominees were revealed. A 12-member expert panel made the call, with each member ranking five candidates and handing out five points down to one. All four go in for their playing careers.

The class takes the Hall of Fame from seven members to 11. The four will be inducted at the HLTV Awards in Belgrade on 9 January 2027, with the show streamed on Twitch and Kick.

dupreeh gets in on his second ballot. He won four Majors with Astralis between 2017 and 2019, then a record fifth with Team Vitality in Paris in 2023, and adds an Intel Grand Slam and seven places in HLTV’s Top 20 Player of the Year list. He announced his retirement from playing in 2025 and has since moved into an analyst role.

NEO is in at the first attempt. He only became eligible this year, after the committee changed the rules that had kept out former players still working in the game in other roles, such as coaching. The Pole dominated the 1.6 era and later won a Major with Virtus.pro at EMS One Katowice 2014. Sudhen “Bleh” Wahengbam, quoted in HLTV’s announcement, calls him “the greatest 1.6 player ever alongside f0rest”. Both men feature in our list of the greatest Counter-Strike players of all time .

Ksharp, elected on his third ballot, has been nominated every year the Hall of Fame has existed. The American won two CPL titles and back-to-back WCG medals in Condition Zero and Source.

title: Megaspeed Says Alice Huang Left in August 2025, Two Months After Singapore Police Took Her Passport
content:
Megaspeed, the Singapore cloud company at the centre of the Nvidia scandal, says Alice Huang left the business on 30 August 2025 and “currently has no role with the company”. In a statement on Sunday, reported by The National , the company said it had “retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation”. It also said it “conducts legitimate and lawful business”, and that media reports about it were not backed by verifiable evidence. The exit date Megaspeed has now given, however, falls more than two months after Singapore police impounded her passport during their investigation into the company.

Alice Huang is the businesswoman whose relationship with Jensen Huang preceded his resignation as Nvidia’s chief executive on 12 November. US investigators reportedly suspect her of gathering information for China, which Beijing denies, and no charges against her have been reported. Megaspeed has denied diverting Nvidia chips to China, and the statement does not say what she did at the company before she left.

Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs set out its own timeline on 12 November, which TalkEsport covered in detail . Police and Singapore Customs opened an investigation into Megaspeed in February 2025, over possible false declarations in server purchases. On 24 June 2025, the US Bureau of Industry and Security carried out a post-shipment check at the company with Alice Huang present, and police interviewed her and impounded her passport that same day.

Megaspeed’s date of 30 August 2025 comes 67 days after that interview, at a time when police were still holding her passport. Police only returned it on 26 February 2026, and she left Singapore that day. By then, police had concluded that she gave them information she knew to be inaccurate, and she was given a stern warning and barred from re-entering the country, according to the ministry’s statement .

The timing also matters for the chip deals. The Wall Street Journal reported that Megaspeed arranged nearly $12 billion of advanced chips for Chinese companies between March 2024 and June 2025, a story that has pushed Congress towards new export bills . Megaspeed’s own date puts her departure about two months after the end of the period the Journal examined.

Megaspeed’s statement is the third version of her role to emerge. She was listed as managing director when the company took its current name in March 2023, according to Singapore’s ministry. Reuters reported last week that media reports put the end of that eight-month tenure in October 2023, in a factbox republished by The Standard . Tan, who now signs Megaspeed’s statements as chairman and chief executive, became a director in November 2023, according to the same factbox.

title: Project Helix Is ‘Not a PC’, Xbox Says, and the Component Crisis Is Now Shaping the Next Xbox
content:
Xbox has given its clearest description yet of Project Helix, calling its next console “a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC”. It is “not a PC that can also play console games”, said Jason Ronald, Xbox’s vice president of next generation, in a 25th anniversary magazine Xbox released on 15 November. The magazine came out on the day the original console turned 25, and its Helix feature makes a notable admission. The current component crisis, which is pushing up the price of almost anything with a plug, has changed how the next Xbox is being built.

The magazine was put together by the team behind Xbox Wire, and it is free to read in a digital edition on Xbox Wire , while printed copies were handed out at Xbox FanFest in Seattle. Its Project Helix feature runs across eight pages and includes a tour of the labs where the console is being designed. Most of what follows comes from Ronald’s interview in those pages, which goes well beyond what Xbox said when it revealed Helix at GDC in March.

Ronald described Helix as “the ultimate gaming machine” that removes “the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games”. In his words, players should be able to bring “four generations” of Xbox games and progress with them and have them available instantly, extending the backward compatibility programme Xbox began in 2015. He also said a console should spare players the chores of PC gaming, adding that he does not want to worry about “updating drivers” or configuring settings before he can play.

That focus on simplicity does not mean locking out enthusiasts who like to tinker. “If you’re a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it,” Ronald said. He also wants progress to follow players between devices, so that someone 25 hours into an 80-hour RPG can switch screens and “instantly resume from where I was”. That builds on Xbox Play Anywhere , which already carries purchases and saves between Xbox consoles and Windows PCs.

The clearest preview of how Helix will work is already on sale. Ronald called the ROG Xbox Ally handheld “a precursor to what we’re doing with Helix”, and said player feedback on its Xbox mode had “fundamentally informed and altered our plans”. That feedback covered playing libraries from several storefronts and showing PC and console games together in one library, although Ronald did not say which PC stores Helix will support.

The most revealing passage in the feature concerns the cost of building it. Consoles have historically been the cheapest way into gaming, the magazine notes, but the component crisis is a factor the team could not have foreseen when Helix began, and meeting that challenge has become “a primary driver” of its innovation. “It’s definitely a challenging time,” Ronald said, but he also called it “one of the most exciting times”, because Xbox has to “invent entirely new technology” to keep advancing the state of the art while still making things “accessible and affordable”. Memory prices have been at the centre of that squeeze, and TalkEsport’s investigation into the RAM price lawsuit explains why they have climbed so far.

title: ZmjjKK is the last Seoul champion left as nobody and CHICHOO exit EDG
content:
EDG’s captain and longest-serving player are reportedly set to stay together at Trace Esports.

Four of the five players who lifted the trophy in Seoul are now gone from EDward Gaming. The club announced on Weibo on Friday 13 November that captain Wang “nobody” Senxu leaves with immediate effect, and a second post ten minutes later confirmed the same for Wan “CHICHOO” Shunzhi.

Both had been at EDG since 2021. CHICHOO arrived in May that year, and EDG’s farewell calls him the player who stayed at the club the longest. nobody joined in September as an initiator and later took over as captain and in-game leader, a path the club’s post traces from young newcomer to the man holding the team together.

The pair were in the lineup for the grand final at Champions Seoul on 25 August 2024, when EDG came back from losing Haven to beat Team Heretics 3-2 and become the first Chinese team to win an international Valorant event.

That season EDG also won China Kickoff, Stage 1 and Stage 2. In 2026 they won Stage 1 and finished third at Masters London, but a 9th-10th place in the Stage 2 Play-Ins and a group stage exit at Champions Shanghai ended the year.

From the Seoul lineup, S1Mon left in August 2025, and Zhang “Smoggy” Zhao signed for Bilibili Gaming on Wednesday. Head coach Muggle, who led the team in Seoul, left in September 2025.

title: molodoy on FalleN: “Every day he says he’s leaving for sure”
content:
FURIA’s AWPer says the team are not looking at anyone to replace their captain, after winning BLAST Rivals in Hong Kong.

The big question hanging over FURIA ‘s season is whether FalleN will really stop at the end of the year. According to his AWPer, Danil “ molodoy ” Golubenko, the captain answers it himself every day.

molodoy spoke in Russian in a short interview filmed in the Hong Kong arena after FURIA won BLAST Rivals 2026 Season 2 on Sunday, with his medal still around his neck. Talking about FalleN, he left little room for a change of heart. In our translation from Russian:

He says it’s set in stone. 100%, every day he says he’s leaving for sure. […] I don’t know, maybe something will change. I can’t predict his thoughts either, but if he stays, it’ll be a plus vibe. If not, it’ll be a minus vibe.

The interviewer then asked whether FURIA were already considering anyone for FalleN’s spot, without naming names. molodoy’s answer: “No, not considering anyone. At all. It’s quiet for now.”

The comments land a day after FalleN’s own interview on BLAST’s broadcast following the semi-final win over Falcons. There, the 2016 Major winner said he had gone months this year without the energy or the passion to give his best, and that he only found that drive again for the final stretch, as we wrote on Sunday .

title: Worlds 2026 : Viper veut devenir « le meilleur ADC de tous les temps »
content:
Deux ans après sa défaite cruelle face à T1 en finale des Worlds 2024, Bilibili Gaming tient enfin sa revanche. Samedi soir, au Barclays Center de Brooklyn, la formation chinoise a renversé Gen.G (3-1) pour décrocher son premier titre mondial et ramener la Coupe de l’Invocateur en LPL, cinq ans après le sacre d’EDward Gaming. Un parcours exceptionnel, marqué par des victoires contre les quatre représentants sud-coréens : Hanwha Life, Dplus KIA, T1 et enfin Gen.G.

Après ce triomphe, les champions du monde ont livré leurs premières impressions en conférence de presse. Pour Bin, déjà finaliste malheureux en 2020 et 2024, cette victoire récompense plusieurs années de persévérance. « Je veux me remercier d’avoir tenu aussi longtemps. J’ai traversé beaucoup d’échecs et de déceptions, mais j’ai continué à avancer et, finalement, j’ai gagné. » Le toplaner n’a pas non plus perdu son humour. Interrogé sur son sommeil après avoir confié ne pas réussir à dormir à la suite de la finale perdue en 2024, il a répondu : « Je suis tellement heureux que je pense que je ne vais pas dormir cette nuit non plus. »

Déjà champion du monde en 2021 avec EDward Gaming, Viper rejoint un cercle très fermé en décrochant un deuxième titre avec une organisation différente. Mais l’ADC sud-coréen de 26 ans ne compte pas s’arrêter là. « Je pense qu’il me reste encore beaucoup de chemin à parcourir pour devenir le meilleur ADC de tous les temps. Il y aura d’autres Worlds, d’autres histoires à écrire. Si je peux décrocher un troisième, puis un quatrième titre, je pense qu’un jour je pourrai devenir le plus grand ADC de l’histoire. » Une ambition assumée après une année particulièrement éprouvante, durant laquelle le joueur reconnaît avoir parfois envisagé d’abandonner.

WORLD CHAMPION ONCE AGAIN. pic.twitter.com/bXl1rMgFPh

Élu MVP de cette grande finale, Knight a lui aussi savouré sa revanche sur les pronostics. « Avant le match, beaucoup de gens nous sous-estimaient. Ils pensaient que je ne pouvais pas battre Chovy et que BLG ne pouvait pas battre Gen.G. Mais nous l’avons fait. Maintenant, je peux enfin dire que nous sommes la meilleure équipe. » De son côté, XUN a insisté sur les difficultés traversées par le collectif : « En 2024, nous avions beaucoup de regrets, car nous étions si proches du titre. Je suis très heureux que nous ayons pu écrire un nouveau chapitre de notre histoire cette année. »

Derrière cette victoire, l’entraîneur Daeny a également souligné l’importance de la préparation stratégique. Face à une équipe de Gen.G réputée pour la profondeur de son champion pool, le technicien a finalement choisi de privilégier les forces de ses propres joueurs, notamment les mages sur la botlane. Il estime également que BLG possédait une longueur d’avance sur les formations coréennes dans sa compréhension du patch, particulièrement concernant la valeur du buff Nashor et les changements apportés à la Téléportation.

title: Apex Legends Revenant guide: how to play Season 31’s biggest winner
content:
Shadow Pounce is back every 15 seconds, the ultimate no longer has a time cap, and three new upgrades reward the player who finishes the fight. Here is how to use all of it.

You crack a shield, the enemy drops behind a rock, and by the time you have run round it they have healed and their team has arrived. Every Apex Legends player loses fights that way, and Revenant is the Legend built to stop it. His passive shows you who is weak, his tactical throws you at them, and his ultimate lets you survive the landing.

For most of 2026 he still was not worth picking. EA’s own chart in the Cipher Designer’s Notes shows the share of players maining him falling from between 7 and 8% around the end of 2025 to 2% by 1 October 2026, and the developers name the cause themselves: his popularity “really dropped off with the rise of other legends like Axle and Pathfinder”, and his upgrades “weren’t very interesting”.

Season 31, Cipher, which went live on Tuesday 3 November 2026, fixes both problems. The two old cooldown upgrades are now part of his base kit, and three new upgrades take their place. Ten days later he is the second most played Legend on apexlegendsstatus.com. This guide covers what changed, how each ability works, which upgrades to take, how to play him in Ranked and public matches, who to play him with, and how to beat him. The rest of the patch is in everything new in Season 31 .

EA’s dev note in the Cipher patch notes is short: the team wanted to give Revenant “more interesting choices” with his upgrades, so it added three new ones and moved the removed ones into his base kit. In practice that means you start every match with what used to take two level ups.

Nothing was taken away. A Season 30 Revenant who picked both cooldown upgrades had a 15 second pounce and a 150 second ultimate. A Season 31 Revenant has those numbers the moment he leaves the dropship, and then gets to choose something new on top.

title: Nvidia Director Mark Stevens Sold $946 Million of Stock Two Months Before Jensen Huang’s Exit
content:
Nvidia director Mark Stevens sold about 4.2 million Nvidia shares worth roughly $946 million between 31 August and 18 September, according to three Form 4 filings with the US Securities and Exchange Commission . The sales came about two months before Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive, and before Nvidia’s shares peaked on 6 October. None of the filings marks the trades as made under a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan, the pre-arranged schedules that many insiders use to sell. Stevens still holds about 27.5 million shares, and Nvidia has not commented on the sales.

There is no suggestion in the filings that the sales were linked to the scandal that later engulfed Huang. Stevens is one of Nvidia’s longest-serving directors and has sold large blocks before, and the trades began days after Nvidia reported its second-quarter results in late August, when company trading windows usually open. The timing has still drawn attention because of what followed. Within weeks, press inquiries about Huang’s ties to Megaspeed and Alice Huang were reaching Nvidia’s leadership, and by 12 November he had resigned .

The first filing covers sales from 31 August to 2 September, when Stevens sold about 1.85 million shares for roughly $411 million at prices between $220 and $226. A second filing covers 3 and 4 September, adding about 1.02 million shares for around $236 million as the price climbed above $234. The third and largest single block came on 18 September, when he sold 1.366 million shares for about $300 million at close to $220. Across the three filings, TalkEsport’s calculation from the reported weighted average prices gives a total of $946.6 million.

All of the shares came from the Third Millennium Trust, which Stevens and his wife run as co-trustees, according to the filings. The trust’s Nvidia holding fell from about 5.2 million shares to just under one million over those three weeks. Stevens still holds about 11.5 million shares directly and 15 million through a second vehicle, the Envy Trust, of which he is trustee. A lawyer signed each filing on his behalf as attorney-in-fact.

The unticked 10b5-1 box is the detail that stands out. Since 2023, insiders have had to flag on Form 4 whether a trade was made under such a plan, which lets them schedule sales in advance and gives them a defence against insider trading claims. Directors can still sell without one during open trading windows, provided they do not hold material non-public information. Interim chief executive Colette Kress, by contrast, sold about $7.6 million of shares in September under a plan adopted in June, according to a tally of 2026 filings.

Stevens is not a newcomer to the board. He has been a director since 2008, after an earlier spell from 1993 to 2006, according to Nvidia’s 2026 proxy statement . Before that, he spent almost two decades as a managing partner at Sequoia Capital, one of Nvidia’s original backers. He now runs S-Cubed Capital, his family’s investment office, and sits on the board’s compensation committee and its nominating and governance committee.

title: Lawmakers Push Tighter AI Chip Export Curbs After Report Megaspeed Arranged $12 Billion in Chips for China
content:
US lawmakers are moving to tighten controls on AI chip exports after a Wall Street Journal report on Megaspeed, the Singapore-based Nvidia partner at the centre of the Jensen Huang scandal. The company arranged nearly $12 billion worth of advanced chips for Chinese companies, the Journal said.

According to records reviewed by the Journal, the arrangements ran from March 2024 to June 2025, and they have raised fears that US export rules were broken or sidestepped. House Speaker Mike Johnson said there is “a developing consensus in Congress” on limiting chip exports to China, Reuters reported . Megaspeed has denied diverting Nvidia chips to China, and Nvidia has said it complies with US law.

Megaspeed’s former chief executive, Alice Huang, is the businesswoman whose relationship with Huang preceded his resignation from Nvidia on 12 November. Reuters reported on Saturday that Huang told Nvidia’s general counsel that his dealings with her and Megaspeed were standard business. The bills now gaining support in Washington, however, go well beyond one company or one executive. Together, they would change how the US polices where its most advanced chips end up and who can use them.

The Journal’s figures point to a model that current rules struggle to reach. Megaspeed bought at least $4.8 billion of AI equipment in under two years and installed it in Southeast Asian facilities, mostly in Malaysia, then rented out the computing power remotely, according to the records it reviewed. The newspaper described that structure as legal on its face. US export rules restrict shipping advanced chips to China, but they have not stopped Chinese companies from renting the same chips in data centres abroad.

Separate reporting points to physical diversion as well. A Chinese company linked to Megaspeed put smuggled Nvidia hardware into service at a Shanghai data centre, according to documents reported by Bloomberg. The equipment was worth about 485 million yuan (around $73 million) and included 52 Super Micro servers fitted with H100 or H200 processors. Both chips are barred from sale to China, although TalkEsport has not seen the documents.

Megaspeed has rejected the claims that it rerouted chips. In a statement dated 12 November , chairman and chief executive Tan Yong Pong said the company had cooperated with inspections by the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security . He added that Megaspeed had hired a US law firm to count its GPUs and check its compliance. Senator Tom Cotton had already urged the Commerce Secretary to investigate Megaspeed for skirting export laws.

title: Jensen Huang Told Nvidia’s Top Lawyer His Alice Huang Ties Were ‘Standard Business’, Reuters Reports
content:
Jensen Huang repeatedly told Nvidia’s most senior executives that his dealings with Alice Huang were ordinary business, according to a Reuters report published on Saturday. Citing two people familiar with the matter and internal correspondence, Reuters said Huang misled general counsel Tim Teter and chief marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld about the relationship before it became public.

The agency also released photos it had verified of the pair together in Taipei in June 2024, adding to images that place them at events since December 2023. Nvidia and a representative for Huang declined to comment, Teter did not respond, and Wagonfeld did not immediately respond.

The report lands two days after Huang resigned as president and chief executive, with chief financial officer Colette Kress taking over on an interim basis, according to Nvidia’s announcement . Alice Huang is a former senior executive of Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based Nvidia customer whose dealings in restricted chips are under scrutiny, and Singapore has since barred her from re-entering the country . Despite the shared surname, the two are not related. Huang acknowledged an affair in a statement on 8 November, apologising to his wife, their children and the company without naming her.

According to Reuters, the questions first reached Nvidia’s leadership through the press. Queries in autumn 2025 and again in October 2026 about Huang’s dealings with Megaspeed and Alice Huang drew the attention of senior executives. On both occasions, Huang described the interactions as appropriate. In two separate messages in October, which Reuters reviewed, he said they reflected “standard business dealings with customers”.

Reuters did not review the 2025 messages, and it did not publish the October exchanges in full. Its sources said that in other messages, Huang also affirmed that his interactions with Megaspeed were routine. The agency did not say whether any executive questioned his account at the time, or when Teter and Wagonfeld learned the true nature of the relationship.

The New York Times’s October 2025 article on the pair’s public meetings drew a sharper response. Huang discussed taking legal action against the paper with Nvidia leaders, according to Reuters’ sources, although neither he nor the company filed a lawsuit. A Times spokesperson told Reuters the paper had received no legal demand. At that stage, Reuters reported, Huang did not describe the relationship as an affair.

title: Kronten Files FIR Against TAG Manager, Plays Jonathan’s Father Call and Claims ₹2 Crore Home Help
content:
GodLike Esports co-owner Chetan “Kronten” Chandgude has filed an FIR against a Team Apex Gaming (TAG) manager he previously accused of spying on GodLike. He also played two recordings on a live stream that he says back up his account of Jonathan’s exit. In the 72-minute stream on his Kronten Gaming YouTube channel on Saturday evening, he claimed that he gave Jonathan ₹2 crore to buy a home soon after he joined GodLike. He said he also arranged a 4BHK flat in Kharghar, Navi Mumbai, at a below-market rate through a builder. TalkEsport has not seen the FIR, and Jonathan, TAG and the manager have not issued a formal response to the new claims.

The stream follows through on what Kronten promised a week earlier. In his first broadcast on 7 November, he said an FIR had been registered without saying against whom, as TalkEsport reported in its breakdown of that stream . He also called an unnamed manager a “spy” inside GodLike, and said he would play a recording of a Christmas call about a “50-50” split “when the time comes”. Jonathan has since called the earlier allegations “completely wrong” . According to Indian esports insiders , the manager named in the FIR is now part of TAG, as are former GodLike player Hades and creator Sharkshe.

The longer of the two recordings runs to about 13 minutes and is dated 25 December 2025, in the early hours of the morning in Kharghar. Kronten said he had called Jonathan to wish him a happy Christmas after two to three months without contact. Jonathan’s father returned the call, and Kronten said someone with him recorded it for safety. On the recording, Kronten tells the father that Jonathan’s 33% stake in GodLike is not going anywhere. He then offers to raise it to 50% if he is repaid for the four years of funding he says he put in.

The two men then disagree about who owns the company. According to the recording, Jonathan’s father argues that GodLike would have four partners, while Kronten insists that the partners are Jonathan, co-owner Amar and himself. Kronten also warns that he will make the split public if the dispute escalates. At one point the father defends his son’s value to the organisation. “What Jonathan did, nobody else can do,” he says.

Kronten used the rest of the segment to dispute the idea that Jonathan carried GodLike. He claimed that Jonathan’s salary rose steadily over three years, from the ₹80,000 a month he said Jonathan was paid on joining, and that he also provided the ₹2 crore and the Kharghar flat. He said Jonathan had taken about ₹70 lakh from him in total, including interest, that GodLike is still loss-making, and that he is willing to share bank statements. He dismissed reports of ₹100 crore brand deals, and claimed that Jonathan never followed GodLike or Amar on social media, mentioned the organisation in his bio or wore its jersey at events.

The second recording features Hades, and Kronten said it was made with his permission. In it, Hades describes a conversation outside the Marriott hotel in Goa. He claims someone there said, “We have access to everything”, and added that “Johnny is with us too”. The speaker is not named in the clips that have circulated, and TalkEsport cannot verify the conversation.
